questions.question:
The graph of a relation is shown below.

Which type of relationship does the graph represent?
questions.answer:
**Vertical line test:** a vertical line to the right of the $y$-axis cuts the graph twice, so some $x$-values have more than one $y$-value (not a function).

**Horizontal line test:** every horizontal line cuts the graph at most once, so each $y$-value comes from only one $x$-value.

So the relation is **one-to-many**. **(B)**

questions.question: Consider the function $f(x) = 4^{x+2}$. What is the derivative of $f(x)$ with respect to $x$?
questions.answer:
Using $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(a^{u}\right) = \ln a \cdot a^{u}\dfrac{du}{dx}$ with $u = x + 2$:
$$f'(x) = \ln 4 \times 4^{x+2}. \quad \textbf{(C)}$$

questions.question:
$A$ and $B$ are two independent events such that $P(\overline{A} \cap B) = 0.4$ and $P(B) = 0.5$.

What is the value of $P(A)$?
questions.answer:
$\overline{A}$ and $B$ are also independent, so
$$P(\overline{A} \cap B) = P(\overline{A})P(B) \implies 0.4 = 0.5\,P(\overline{A}) \implies P(\overline{A}) = 0.8.$$
So $P(A) = 1 - 0.8 = 0.2$. **(B)**

questions.question:
Gemma scored 70 on a test in which the marks were normally distributed with mean 50 and standard deviation 15.

What new mark would Gemma be given if the marks were adjusted to have mean 60 and standard deviation 12?
questions.answer:
Her $z$-score stays the same: $z = \dfrac{70 - 50}{15} = \dfrac43$.

New mark $= 60 + \dfrac43 \times 12 = 76$. **(B)**

questions.question:
The diagram shows a circle with radius $r$ cm and a sector with an internal angle of $30^\circ$.

If the area of the shaded segment is $1.7\text{ cm}^2$, which of the following is closest to the radius of the circle?
questions.answer:
With $\theta = 30^\circ = \dfrac\pi6$:
$$\tfrac12r^2\left(\tfrac\pi6 - \sin\tfrac\pi6\right) = 1.7 \implies r^2\left(\tfrac{\pi}{12} - \tfrac14\right) = 1.7 \implies r^2 \approx 144.06 \implies r \approx 12.00 \text{ cm}. \quad \textbf{(C)}$$

questions.question:
A particle is moving along the $x$-axis. The graph shows its velocity, $v$ metres per second, at time $t$ seconds. The velocity decreases linearly from $10$ m/s at $t = 0$ to $0$ at $t = 5$, and continues to decrease after that.

When $t = 0$, the displacement $x$ is equal to 3 metres. What is the maximum value of the displacement $x$?
questions.answer:
The particle moves in the positive direction until $v = 0$ at $t = 5$, then turns back, so $x$ is greatest at $t = 5$.

$v = 10 - 2t \implies x = 10t - t^2 + C$, and $x(0) = 3$ gives $C = 3$. So $x(5) = 50 - 25 + 3 = 28$ m. (Equivalently, $3 + $ area of the triangle $= 3 + \tfrac12 \times 5 \times 10 = 28$.) **(C)**

questions.question:
A circular Ferris wheel has a diameter of 40 metres and rotates at a constant rate, completing one full revolution every 2 minutes. The height of a certain passenger above ground as a function of time can be modelled by
$$h(t) = 20\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{60}(t - 15)\right) + 30,$$
where $h(t)$ is the height in metres and $t$ is the time in seconds.

What does the parameter 30 in the equation represent in the context of the Ferris wheel?
questions.answer: Adding 30 translates the graph up 30 units: the centre line of the motion, i.e. the centre of the wheel is 30 m above the ground. **(D)**
options: The phase shift in time of the passenger on the Ferris wheel.
The amplitude of the motion of the passenger on the Ferris wheel.
The period of rotation of the Ferris wheel.
The vertical shift of the centre of the Ferris wheel above the ground.

questions.question: Given that $\displaystyle\int_1^6 f(x)\,dx = 6$ and $\displaystyle\int_3^6 f(x)\,dx = -4$, what is the value of $\displaystyle\int_1^3 \big(f(x) + x\big)\,dx$?

The strength of an earthquake is calculated using Richter's formula
$$M = \log_{10}(I),$$
where $M$ is the magnitude of the earthquake and $I$ is the intensity.

An earthquake with a magnitude of $5.4$ was detected in the desert. A second earthquake occurred in the same location a few years later and was measured to be twice as intense as the first earthquake.

What was the magnitude of the second earthquake?
questions.answer:
First earthquake: $\log_{10} I = 5.4$. The second has intensity $2I$:
$$M_2 = \log_{10}(2I) = \log_{10}2 + \log_{10}I = 0.301\ldots + 5.4 \approx 5.7. \quad \textbf{(D)}$$

questions.question: What is the limiting sum of the geometric series $\log_e 2 - (\log_e 2)^2 + (\log_e 2)^3 - (\log_e 2)^4 + \cdots$?
questions.answer:
$a = \ln 2$, $r = -\ln 2$ (and $|r| < 1$):
$$S_\infty = \frac{\ln 2}{1 + \ln 2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\ln e + \ln 2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\ln(2e)} = \log_{2e}2 \quad \text{(change of base).} \quad \textbf{(D)}$$

questions.question: Given $f(x) = \log_{10}\left(3x^2 - 2x\right)$, find the exact value of $f'(2)$.
questions.answer:
Using $\dfrac{d}{dx}\log_a u = \dfrac{u'}{u\ln a}$:
$$f'(x) = \frac{6x - 2}{\left(3x^2 - 2x\right)\ln 10}, \qquad f'(2) = \frac{12 - 2}{(12 - 4)\ln 10} = \frac{10}{8\ln 10} = \frac{5}{4\ln 10}.$$

questions.question:
In a population, 60% of people are of blood type $O$ and 40% are of blood type $A$. Two people are chosen at random from this population.

Complete the tree diagram representing this situation.
questions.answer:
Each person is $A$ with probability $0.4$ and $O$ with probability $0.6$, independently:

- First person $A$ ($0.4$): second $A$ ($0.4$) or $O$ ($0.6$)
- First person $O$ ($0.6$): second $A$ ($0.4$) or $O$ ($0.6$)

Outcomes: $AA = 0.16$, $AO = 0.24$, $OA = 0.24$, $OO = 0.36$.

questions.question: Let $f(x) = 4x^2 - 3x$. Use the definition $f'(x) = \displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$ to find the derivative of $f(x)$.
questions.answer:
$$\begin{aligned}
f(x+h) - f(x) &= 4(x+h)^2 - 3(x+h) - 4x^2 + 3x = 8xh + 4h^2 - 3h,\\
f'(x) &= \lim_{h\to0}\frac{8xh + 4h^2 - 3h}{h} = \lim_{h\to0}(8x + 4h - 3) = 8x - 3.
\end{aligned}$$

questions.question: Solve $\log_5 9 = 2\log_5 12 - \log_5 x$.
questions.answer: $$\log_5 9 = \log_5 144 - \log_5 x = \log_5\frac{144}{x} \implies 9 = \frac{144}{x} \implies x = 16.$$

questions.question: Consider the functions $f(x) = \dfrac1x - 2$ and $g(x) = x + 3$. Let $h(x) = f(g(x))$. Find the domain and range of $h(x)$.
questions.answer:
$$h(x) = f(x + 3) = \frac{1}{x + 3} - 2.$$
**Domain:** $x + 3 \ne 0$, i.e. all real $x \ne -3$.

**Range:** $\dfrac{1}{x+3}$ takes every real value except $0$, so $h(x)$ takes every real value except $-2$: all real $y \ne -2$.

questions.question: Find the derivative of the function $y = \tan\left(x^2\right)$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x\sec^2\left(x^2\right)$.

questions.question: Given that $\dfrac{d}{dx}\tan\left(x^2\right) = 2x\sec^2\left(x^2\right)$, by using an appropriate trigonometric identity, find $\displaystyle\int x\tan^2\left(x^2\right)dx$.
questions.answer:
Using $\tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta - 1$:
$$\int x\tan^2\left(x^2\right)dx = \int x\sec^2\left(x^2\right)dx - \int x\,dx = \frac12\tan\left(x^2\right) - \frac{x^2}{2} + C.$$

prev.question: Find the derivative of the function $y = \tan\left(x^2\right)$.
prev.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x\sec^2\left(x^2\right)$.

questions.question: Show that $\log_e(1 + \sin x) - \log_e(1 - \sin x) = 2\log_e(\sec x + \tan x)$.
questions.answer:
$$\begin{aligned}
\ln(1 + \sin x) - \ln(1 - \sin x) &= \ln\frac{1 + \sin x}{1 - \sin x} = \ln\frac{(1 + \sin x)^2}{(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)} = \ln\frac{(1 + \sin x)^2}{1 - \sin^2 x}\\
&= \ln\frac{(1 + \sin x)^2}{\cos^2 x} = 2\ln\left(\frac{1 + \sin x}{\cos x}\right) = 2\ln(\sec x + \tan x),
\end{aligned}$$
(for $x$ where $\sec x + \tan x > 0$, i.e. where both sides are defined).

questions.question:
Two mountains, $P$ and $Q$, lie directly north of a campground $C$. Cathy walks from $C$ on a bearing of $065^\circ$ a distance of 4 km to a point $T$. The diagram shows the relative positions, viewed from above.

From point $T$, the base of mountain $P$ is on a bearing of $285^\circ$, while the base of mountain $Q$ is on a bearing of $315^\circ$.

Show that $\angle QTC = 70^\circ$.
questions.answer:
The bearing of $C$ from $T$ is $065^\circ + 180^\circ = 245^\circ$. So
$$\angle QTC = 315^\circ - 245^\circ = 70^\circ.$$

questions.question:
Two mountains, $P$ and $Q$, lie directly north of a campground $C$. Cathy walks from $C$ on a bearing of $065^\circ$ a distance of 4 km to a point $T$. The diagram shows the relative positions, viewed from above.

From point $T$, the base of mountain $P$ is on a bearing of $285^\circ$, while the base of mountain $Q$ is on a bearing of $315^\circ$.

Given that $\angle QTC = 70^\circ$, calculate the distance $CQ$, correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle QTC$: $\angle QCT = 65^\circ$, $\angle QTC = 70^\circ$, so $\angle CQT = 45^\circ$. By the sine rule:
$$\frac{CQ}{\sin 70^\circ} = \frac{4}{\sin 45^\circ} \implies CQ = \frac{4\sin 70^\circ}{\sin 45^\circ} = 5.315\ldots \approx 5.3 \text{ km}.$$

Given that $CQ \approx 5.3157$ km, calculate the distance $PQ$.
questions.answer:
$\angle PTC = 285^\circ - 245^\circ = 40^\circ$, and $\angle PCT = 65^\circ$, so $\angle CPT = 75^\circ$. By the sine rule:
$$CP = \frac{4\sin 40^\circ}{\sin 75^\circ} = 2.6618\ldots \text{ km}.$$
$$PQ = CQ - CP = 5.3157\ldots - 2.6618\ldots \approx 2.7 \text{ km}.$$

questions.question:
A semicircle on the number plane is defined by the equation $y = \sqrt{-x^2 + 10x - 16}$.

Find the centre and radius of the semicircle.
questions.answer:
$$y^2 = -x^2 + 10x - 16 \implies x^2 - 10x + 25 + y^2 = 9 \implies (x - 5)^2 + y^2 = 9, \quad y \ge 0.$$
Centre $(5, 0)$, radius $3$.

questions.question:
A semicircle on the number plane is defined by the equation $y = \sqrt{-x^2 + 10x - 16}$.

The semicircle has centre $(5, 0)$ and radius 3. Sketch the curve.
questions.answer: The upper half of the circle: endpoints $(2, 0)$ and $(8, 0)$, highest point $(5, 3)$.

questions.question:
A semicircle on the number plane is defined by the equation $y = \sqrt{-x^2 + 10x - 16}$.

The semicircle has centre $(5, 0)$ and radius 3. Hence or otherwise find $\displaystyle\int_2^8 \sqrt{-x^2 + 10x - 16}\,dx$. Leave your answer in exact form.
questions.answer:
The integral is the area of the whole semicircle of radius 3:
$$\int_2^8\sqrt{-x^2 + 10x - 16}\,dx = \frac12\pi(3)^2 = \frac{9\pi}{2}.$$

questions.question: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_1^3 \frac{24x^2 - 14}{4x^3 - 7x + 5}\,dx$, leaving your answer in simplest exact form.
questions.answer:
The numerator is $2\times\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(4x^3 - 7x + 5\right)$, and the denominator is positive on $[1, 3]$:
$$\int_1^3\frac{24x^2 - 14}{4x^3 - 7x + 5}\,dx = 2\Big[\ln\left(4x^3 - 7x + 5\right)\Big]_1^3 = 2(\ln 92 - \ln 2) = 2\ln 46.$$

questions.question:
The graph of $y = f'(x)$ is shown. It touches the $x$-axis at $x = -1$ (where it has a local maximum of $0$), has a local minimum near $x \approx 2.5$, and crosses the $x$-axis at $x = 4$.

Determine the nature of the point on the curve $y = f(x)$ at $x = -1$. Justify your answer with appropriate mathematical reasoning and reference to the graph.
questions.answer: $f'(-1) = 0$, so there is a stationary point at $x = -1$. From the graph, $f'(x) < 0$ just to the left **and** just to the right of $x = -1$ (the graph of $f'$ only touches the axis there). Since $f'$ does not change sign, the stationary point is a **horizontal (stationary) point of inflection**.

questions.question:
The graph of $y = f'(x)$ is shown. It touches the $x$-axis at $x = -1$ (where it has a local maximum of $0$), has a local minimum near $x \approx 2.5$, and crosses the $x$-axis at $x = 4$.

Sketch a possible graph for $y = f(x)$, showing any stationary points or turning points.
questions.answer:
- $f'(x) < 0$ for $x < 4$ (except $x = -1$): $f$ is decreasing, with a **horizontal point of inflection** at $x = -1$.
- $f'(x) > 0$ for $x > 4$: $f$ is increasing, so there is a **minimum turning point** at $x = 4$.

(The vertical position of the curve is not determined.)

questions.question: Find the equation of the normal to the curve $y = \dfrac{\log_e(x+2)}{x+2}$ at the point $(-1, 0)$.
questions.answer:
By the quotient rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{(x+2)\cdot\frac{1}{x+2} - \ln(x+2)}{(x+2)^2} = \frac{1 - \ln(x+2)}{(x+2)^2}.$$
At $x = -1$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - \ln 1}{1} = 1$, so the normal has gradient $-1$:
$$y - 0 = -(x + 1) \implies y = -x - 1.$$

The rectangle's height is $180 + 80 + 190 = 450$ m, so its area is $700 \times 450 = 315\,000\ \text{m}^2$.

Widths of the lake: $80$ (left), $450 - 80 - 70 = 300$ (middle), $100$ (right). Trapezoidal rule with $h = 350$:
$$A_{\text{lake}} \approx \frac{350}{2}\left[80 + 2(300) + 100\right] = 175 \times 780 = 136\,500\ \text{m}^2.$$
$$P(\text{lake}) \approx \frac{136\,500}{315\,000} = \frac{13}{30} \approx 0.43.$$

questions.question:
The graph of $y = \log_e x$ is shown on a grid.

Sketch the curve $y = \dfrac{\log_e(x + 3)}{2}$ on the same diagram, showing the intercepts and asymptotes.
questions.answer:
- Vertical asymptote: $x = -3$.
- $x$-intercept: $\ln(x + 3) = 0 \implies x = -2$, i.e. $(-2, 0)$.
- $y$-intercept: $y = \tfrac12\ln 3 \approx 0.55$, i.e. $\left(0, \tfrac12\ln 3\right)$.

questions.question:
The graph of $y = \log_e x$ is shown on a grid.

Explain the transformations that map $y = \log_e x$ onto $y = \dfrac{\log_e(x + 3)}{2}$.
questions.answer: A **horizontal translation 3 units to the left** (replace $x$ by $x + 3$), followed by a **vertical dilation by a factor of $\tfrac12$** (multiply $y$ by $\tfrac12$). (These two can be done in either order.)

questions.question:
The graph shows the displacement $x$ of a particle moving along a straight line as a function of time $t$. Point $A$ is on the part of the curve that is increasing and concave up (below the point of inflection).

Describe the motion of the particle at the point $A$: is it speeding up or slowing down? Make reference to the velocity and acceleration of the particle.
questions.answer:
At $A$ the gradient of the displacement–time graph is positive, so the **velocity is positive**. The graph is concave up at $A$, so $\ddot x > 0$: the **acceleration is positive**.

Velocity and acceleration have the same sign, so the particle is **speeding up**.

questions.question:
Consider the gradient function $f'(x) = 3(x - 5)(x - 1)$. The graph of $y = f(x)$ passes through the point $(2, 16)$.

Given that $f(x) = x^3 - 9x^2 + 15x + 14$, show that a point of inflection exists at $(3, 5)$.
questions.answer:
$f''(x) = 6x - 18 = 0 \iff x = 3$, and $f(3) = 27 - 81 + 45 + 14 = 5$.

$f''(x) < 0$ for $x < 3$ and $f''(x) > 0$ for $x > 3$, so the concavity changes at $x = 3$: there is a point of inflection at $(3, 5)$.

Given that $f(x) = x^3 - 9x^2 + 15x + 14$, find the maximum and minimum values of $f(x)$ in the interval $-2 \le x \le 6$. You do not need to determine the nature of the stationary points.

Consider the gradient function $f'(x) = 3(x - 5)(x - 1)$. The graph of $y = f(x)$ passes through the point $(2, 16)$.

Given that $f(x) = x^3 - 9x^2 + 15x + 14$, show that a point of inflection exists at $(3, 5)$.
prev.answer:
$f''(x) = 6x - 18 = 0 \iff x = 3$, and $f(3) = 27 - 81 + 45 + 14 = 5$.

$f''(x) < 0$ for $x < 3$ and $f''(x) > 0$ for $x > 3$, so the concavity changes at $x = 3$: there is a point of inflection at $(3, 5)$.

questions.question:
The discrete random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given in the table below.

| $x$ | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X = x)$ | 0.3 | $a$ | $b$ | 0.1 |

Find the values of $a$ and $b$, given $\mu = 3.1$.
questions.answer:
Probabilities sum to 1: $\;0.3 + a + b + 0.1 = 1 \implies a + b = 0.6$.

Mean: $\;2(0.3) + 3a + 4b + 5(0.1) = 3.1 \implies 3a + 4b = 2$.

Substituting $a = 0.6 - b$: $\;1.8 + b = 2 \implies b = 0.2$, $a = 0.4$.

questions.question:
The probability density function of a random variable $X$ is given by
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{-\sin(\ln x)}{kx}, & e^{-\pi} \le x \le 1 \\[2mm] 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

Show that $k = 2$.
questions.answer:
The total probability is 1. Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\cos(\ln x) = -\dfrac{\sin(\ln x)}{x}$:
$$\int_{e^{-\pi}}^{1}\frac{-\sin(\ln x)}{kx}\,dx = \frac1k\Big[\cos(\ln x)\Big]_{e^{-\pi}}^{1} = \frac1k\left(\cos 0 - \cos(-\pi)\right) = \frac{2}{k} = 1 \implies k = 2.$$

questions.question:
The probability density function of a random variable $X$ is given by
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{-\sin(\ln x)}{kx}, & e^{-\pi} \le x \le 1 \\[2mm] 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

Given that $k = 2$, find $P\left(X < \dfrac\pi4\right)$. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
questions.answer:
$e^{-\pi} < \frac\pi4 < 1$, so
$$P\left(X < \tfrac\pi4\right) = \frac12\Big[\cos(\ln x)\Big]_{e^{-\pi}}^{\pi/4} = \frac12\left(\cos\left(\ln\tfrac\pi4\right) + 1\right) \approx 0.985.$$

questions.question:
An electric battery is being recharged. The capacity, $C$%, of the battery while charging at time $t$ minutes may be modelled by the equation
$$C = 100\left(1 - 2^{-kt}\right).$$
The battery is charged to 35% capacity after 50 minutes.

Show that the value of $k$ is $0.01243$, correct to 4 significant figures.
questions.answer: $$35 = 100\left(1 - 2^{-50k}\right) \implies 2^{-50k} = 0.65 \implies -50k\ln 2 = \ln 0.65 \implies k = \frac{-\ln 0.65}{50\ln 2} = 0.012430\ldots \approx 0.01243.$$

questions.question:
An electric battery is being recharged. The capacity, $C$%, of the battery while charging at time $t$ minutes may be modelled by the equation
$$C = 100\left(1 - 2^{-kt}\right).$$
The battery is charged to 35% capacity after 50 minutes.

Given $k \approx 0.01243$: to prolong the service life of the battery, the charger may be set to switch off when the battery reaches 90% capacity. For how long will the battery be on charge until it reaches 90% capacity? Give your answer in hours and minutes, correct to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
$$90 = 100\left(1 - 2^{-kt}\right) \implies 2^{-kt} = 0.1 \implies t = \frac{\ln 10}{k\ln 2} \approx 267.3 \text{ min}.$$
About **4 hours 27 minutes**.

questions.question:
An electric battery is being recharged. The capacity, $C$%, of the battery while charging at time $t$ minutes may be modelled by the equation
$$C = 100\left(1 - 2^{-kt}\right).$$
The battery is charged to 35% capacity after 50 minutes.

By considering the first and second derivatives, describe the behaviour of $C$ for $t \ge 0$ if the battery is left on charge indefinitely.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{dC}{dt} = 100k\ln 2\cdot2^{-kt} > 0, \qquad \frac{d^2C}{dt^2} = -100(k\ln 2)^2\,2^{-kt} < 0.$$
So $C$ is always increasing, but at a decreasing rate (the charging slows down). As $t \to \infty$, $2^{-kt} \to 0$, so $C \to 100$: the battery approaches full capacity but never quite reaches it.

questions.question:
A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement $x$, in metres, from a fixed point $O$ is given by
$$x = 1 - 2\sin\left(2t + \frac\pi6\right),$$
where $t$ is measured in seconds from $t = 0$.

Where is the particle initially?
questions.answer: At $t = 0$: $x = 1 - 2\sin\frac\pi6 = 1 - 1 = 0$. The particle starts at $O$.

questions.question:
A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement $x$, in metres, from a fixed point $O$ is given by
$$x = 1 - 2\sin\left(2t + \frac\pi6\right),$$
where $t$ is measured in seconds from $t = 0$.

When and where does the particle first come to rest?
questions.answer:
$v = \dot x = -4\cos\left(2t + \frac\pi6\right) = 0 \implies 2t + \frac\pi6 = \frac\pi2$ (first time) $\implies t = \frac\pi6$ s.

Then $x = 1 - 2\sin\frac\pi2 = -1$: the particle first comes to rest after $\frac\pi6$ seconds, **1 m to the left of $O$** ($x = -1$).

questions.question:
A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement $x$, in metres, from a fixed point $O$ is given by
$$x = 1 - 2\sin\left(2t + \frac\pi6\right),$$
where $t$ is measured in seconds from $t = 0$.

The particle starts at $O$ and first comes to rest at $x = -1$ when $t = \dfrac\pi6$. Calculate how far the particle has travelled at time $t = \dfrac{7\pi}{24}$. Give your answer as an exact value.
questions.answer:
At $t = \frac{7\pi}{24}$: $2t + \frac\pi6 = \frac{3\pi}{4}$, so $x = 1 - 2\sin\frac{3\pi}{4} = 1 - \sqrt2$.

The particle next stops when $2t + \frac\pi6 = \frac{3\pi}{2}$, i.e. $t = \frac{2\pi}{3} > \frac{7\pi}{24}$, so between $t = \frac\pi6$ and $t = \frac{7\pi}{24}$ it moves only to the right.

Distance $= |{-1} - 0| + |(1 - \sqrt2) - (-1)| = 1 + (2 - \sqrt2) = 3 - \sqrt2$ m.

questions.question:
A quadratic has equation $y = A + Bx - x^2$. When the function is reflected in the $y$-axis, the result is identical to a horizontal translation of the original function by $-3$ (i.e. 3 units to the left).

Given that the curve meets the $y$-axis at $(0, 18)$, determine the area of the region bounded by the curve and the $x$-axis.
questions.answer:
Reflection in the $y$-axis: $y = A - Bx - x^2$. Translation 3 left: $y = A + B(x + 3) - (x + 3)^2 = (A + 3B - 9) + (B - 6)x - x^2$.

Equating coefficients: $-B = B - 6 \implies B = 3$ (and then $A + 3B - 9 = A$ ✓). The $y$-intercept gives $A = 18$:
$$y = 18 + 3x - x^2 = -(x - 6)(x + 3).$$
$$\text{Area} = \int_{-3}^{6}\left(18 + 3x - x^2\right)dx = \left[18x + \frac{3x^2}{2} - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-3}^{6} = 90 - (-31.5) = \frac{243}{2} \text{ square units}.$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows two concentric circles, one with radius $r\sqrt r$ and the other with radius $r$. The shaded region is bounded by two radii of the larger circle that make an angle of $\dfrac\pi3$ at the centre, the arc of the larger circle between them, and the chord of the smaller circle joining the points where those radii cross it.

Show that $A_{\text{shaded}} = \dfrac\pi6r^3 - \dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}r^2$.
questions.answer:
Shaded area $=$ (sector of the larger circle) $-$ (triangle formed by the centre and the chord of the smaller circle):
$$A = \frac12\left(r\sqrt r\right)^2\cdot\frac\pi3 - \frac12r^2\sin\frac\pi3 = \frac{\pi}{6}r^3 - \frac{\sqrt3}{4}r^2.$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows two concentric circles, one with radius $r\sqrt r$ and the other with radius $r$. The shaded region is bounded by two radii of the larger circle that make an angle of $\dfrac\pi3$ at the centre, the arc of the larger circle between them, and the chord of the smaller circle joining the points where those radii cross it.

Given that $A_{\text{shaded}} = \dfrac\pi6r^3 - \dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}r^2$, find the value of $r$ at which the area of the shaded region is a minimum.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{dA}{dr} = \frac{\pi}{2}r^2 - \frac{\sqrt3}{2}r = \frac r2\left(\pi r - \sqrt3\right) = 0 \implies r = \frac{\sqrt3}{\pi} \quad (r > 0).$$
$$\frac{d^2A}{dr^2} = \pi r - \frac{\sqrt3}{2} = \sqrt3 - \frac{\sqrt3}{2} > 0 \text{ at } r = \frac{\sqrt3}{\pi},$$
so this is a minimum: $r = \dfrac{\sqrt3}{\pi}$.

questions.question:
Taylor is purchasing an apartment for \$1 562 500. She pays a 20% deposit and will borrow the remaining amount. The loan has an annual interest rate of 5.4% compounded monthly and a monthly account-keeping fee of \$10, which is added to the balance after the interest is applied each month. The loan plus the account fee is to be repaid over 30 years with equal monthly repayments.

Find the total amount that Taylor will have spent in purchasing the apartment and outline two things she could do to reduce this amount.
questions.answer:
Deposit $= 0.2 \times 1\,562\,500 = \$312\,500$; loan $P = \$1\,250\,000$. Monthly rate $r = 0.0045$, $n = 360$, repayment $M$.

After each month the balance is multiplied by $1.0045$, then $10$ is added and $M$ is taken off, so with $R = M - 10$:
$$A_n = P(1.0045)^n - R\left(1 + 1.0045 + \cdots + 1.0045^{n-1}\right) = P(1.0045)^n - R\,\frac{1.0045^n - 1}{0.0045}.$$
Setting $A_{360} = 0$:
$$R = \frac{1\,250\,000 \times 0.0045 \times 1.0045^{360}}{1.0045^{360} - 1} \approx 7019.13 \implies M \approx \$7029.13.$$
Total spent $= 312\,500 + 360 \times 7029.13 \approx \$2\,842\,989$.

To reduce this she could, for example: pay a larger deposit (borrow less); make larger or more frequent repayments to pay the loan off sooner; find a lower interest rate or a loan with no account-keeping fee.

questions.question: The graph of a relation is shown below. What type of relationship does the graph represent?
questions.answer: A vertical line near the $y$-axis cuts the graph three times, so some $x$-values have several $y$-values; every horizontal line cuts it only once, so each $y$-value has one $x$-value. The relation is **one-to-many**. **(B)**

questions.question:
A function $f(x)$ is such that
$$\int_{-k}^{k}f(x)\,dx = 2\int_0^k f(x)\,dx.$$
Which of the following could be a possible function for $f(x)$?
questions.answer: The property holds for **even** functions. $\cos 2x$ is even; $\sin 2x$, $\tan 2x$ and $\operatorname{cosec}2x$ are odd. **(B)**

questions.question:
A die is rolled twice. Let events $X$ and $Y$ be:
- $X$: the first roll is a 1;
- $Y$: the sum of the two rolls is 7.

Which of the following statements is true?
questions.answer: $P(X) = \frac16$, $P(Y) = \frac{6}{36} = \frac16$, and $X \cap Y = \{(1, 6)\}$ so $P(X \cap Y) = \frac{1}{36} = P(X)P(Y)$. The events are independent. **(A)**
options: Event $X$ is a subset of event $Y$.
The probabilities of events $X$ and $Y$ are different.

questions.question: Ben scored 53 on a test where the scores were normally distributed with a mean of 41 and a standard deviation of 7.5. If the scores are adjusted to have a new mean of 44 and a new standard deviation of 6, what would Ben's adjusted score be, to the nearest whole number?
Let $f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2$. In which domain is the function decreasing and concave down?
questions.answer: $f'(x) = 3x(x - 2) < 0$ for $0 < x < 2$ (decreasing); $f''(x) = 6x - 6 < 0$ for $x < 1$ (concave down). Both: $(0, 1)$. **(B)**

questions.question: A regular hexagon is inscribed inside a circle with centre $O$. $A$ and $B$ are adjacent vertices of the hexagon. Given the area of $\triangle ABO = 14\text{ cm}^2$, what is the perimeter of the hexagon to the nearest centimetre?
questions.answer: $\triangle ABO$ is equilateral with side $s$ (the hexagon's side). $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2 = 14 \implies s^2 = \frac{56}{\sqrt3} \implies s \approx 5.686$. Perimeter $= 6s \approx 34.1$ cm. **(C)**

questions.question: If $f(x) = \sqrt x$ and $g(x) = \ln(x - 1)$, what is the domain of the composite function $f(g(x))$?
questions.answer: $f(g(x)) = \sqrt{\ln(x - 1)}$ needs $x > 1$ and $\ln(x - 1) \ge 0$, i.e. $x - 1 \ge 1$, so $x \ge 2$. **(D)**

questions.question:
A probability density function is given by
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} x - 1, & 1 \le x \le a \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere.} \end{cases}$$
Which one of the following is the correct way to find the value of $a$?
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int_1^a(x - 1)\,dx = \frac{(a-1)^2}{2} = 1 \implies a^2 - 2a - 1 = 0$, and $a > 1$, so take the larger root. **(A)**

questions.question: Which of the following functions best represents the graph below? (The branches cross the $x$-axis at $x = \pm\frac\pi4, \pm\frac{3\pi}{4}$, with vertical asymptotes at $x = 0, \pm\frac\pi2, \pm\pi$, and each branch is increasing.)
questions.answer: Asymptotes are $\frac\pi2$ apart, so the period is $\frac\pi2$ and the coefficient of $x$ is 2. There is an asymptote at $x = 0$: $2(0) + c = \frac\pi2 \implies c = \frac\pi2$ (check: zeros where $2x + \frac\pi2 = k\pi$, i.e. $x = \pm\frac\pi4, \ldots$). **(C)**

questions.question: The function $f(x) = e^x$ is transformed by a horizontal translation of $\log_e 2$ units in the negative $x$ direction, followed by a horizontal dilation of scale factor 2. What is the new function $g(x)$?
questions.answer: Translation: $e^{x + \ln 2} = 2e^x$. Horizontal dilation by factor 2 (replace $x$ by $\frac x2$): $g(x) = 2e^{x/2}$. **(A)**

questions.question: Evaluate $x$ when $x = \log_{31}32 \times \log_{30}31 \times \log_{29}30 \times \cdots \times \log_2 3$, for $x \in \mathbb{Z}$.
questions.answer:
Change every log to base $e$; the product telescopes:
$$x = \frac{\ln 32}{\ln 31}\times\frac{\ln 31}{\ln 30}\times\cdots\times\frac{\ln 3}{\ln 2} = \frac{\ln 32}{\ln 2} = \log_2 32 = 5.$$

questions.question:
Given the equation of a circle: $x^2 - 4x + y^2 + 2y - 4 = 0$.

Determine the centre and radius.

Given the equation of a circle: $x^2 - 4x + y^2 + 2y - 4 = 0$.

The circle has centre $(2, -1)$ and radius 3. The line $y = mx + 2$ is a tangent to the circle. Determine the values of $m$.
questions.answer:
Substitute $y = mx + 2$:
$$x^2 - 4x + (mx + 2)^2 + 2(mx + 2) - 4 = 0 \implies (1 + m^2)x^2 + (6m - 4)x + 4 = 0.$$
A tangent meets the circle once, so $\Delta = 0$:
$$(6m - 4)^2 - 16(1 + m^2) = 20m^2 - 48m = 4m(5m - 12) = 0 \implies m = 0 \text{ or } m = \frac{12}{5}.$$

questions.question:
The ages of 26 million residents of Australia are normally distributed with a mean of 45 years and a standard deviation of 11 years.

Calculate how many more people are older than 56 than are older than 67.
questions.answer:
$56 = \mu + \sigma$ and $67 = \mu + 2\sigma$. By the empirical rule, $P(X > 56) = 16\%$ and $P(X > 67) = 2.5\%$.

Difference $= 13.5\% \times 26\,000\,000 = 3\,510\,000$ more people.

Determine the percentage, rounded to the nearest whole number, of individuals under 56 who are also younger than 34.

The subjects that a group of university students take are recorded. Out of the group, 24% of the students do both Statistics ($S$) and Business ($B$), while 10% do neither. In the Venn diagram, $x$ and $y$ are the proportions who take only Statistics and only Business respectively.

It is known that the number of students who take Statistics is twice the number who take Business. Find the values of $x$ and $y$.

The subjects that a group of university students take are recorded. Out of the group, 24% of the students do both Statistics ($S$) and Business ($B$), while 10% do neither. In the Venn diagram, $x$ and $y$ are the proportions who take only Statistics and only Business respectively.

Given $x = 0.52$ and $y = 0.14$: if a student is selected at random, find the probability that they are not taking Statistics given that they are studying Business.
questions.answer: $$P(\overline S \mid B) = \frac{y}{y + 0.24} = \frac{0.14}{0.38} = \frac{7}{19} \approx 0.368.$$

questions.question:
Consider the functions $f(x) = |2x - 4|$ and $g(x) = |x + 1|$.

On the same number plane, sketch the graphs of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, showing all important features.
questions.answer:
- $y = |2x - 4|$: vertex $(2, 0)$, $y$-intercept $4$.
- $y = |x + 1|$: vertex $(-1, 0)$, $y$-intercept $1$.
- They intersect where $2x - 4 = x + 1$ ($x = 5$) and $-(2x - 4) = x + 1$ ($x = 1$): at $(1, 2)$ and $(5, 6)$.

questions.question:
Consider the functions $f(x) = |2x - 4|$ and $g(x) = |x + 1|$.

The graphs intersect at $(1, 2)$ and $(5, 6)$. Use the graphs to solve the inequality $|2x - 4| < |x + 1|$.
questions.answer: $y = |2x - 4|$ lies below $y = |x + 1|$ between the intersection points: $1 < x < 5$.

questions.question: Differentiate and simplify $g(x) = e^x\sin x - e^x\cos x$.
questions.answer: $$g'(x) = e^x\sin x + e^x\cos x - \left(e^x\cos x - e^x\sin x\right) = 2e^x\sin x.$$

questions.question: The derivative of a function is given by $f'(x) = e^x\sin x$. Given that $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(e^x\sin x - e^x\cos x\right) = 2e^x\sin x$, find $f(x)$ if it is known that $f(\pi) = \dfrac{e^\pi}{2}$.
questions.answer:
$$f(x) = \frac12\left(e^x\sin x - e^x\cos x\right) + C.$$
$f(\pi) = \frac12\left(0 + e^\pi\right) + C = \frac{e^\pi}{2} \implies C = 0$. So $f(x) = \dfrac12e^x(\sin x - \cos x)$.

questions.question:
Consider the series $1\tfrac13 + 2\tfrac19 + 4\tfrac{1}{27} + 8\tfrac{1}{81} + \cdots$

Find an expression for the general term.
questions.answer:
Each term is a power of 2 plus a power of $\frac13$:
$$T_n = 2^{n-1} + \left(\frac13\right)^n.$$

questions.question:
Consider the series $1\tfrac13 + 2\tfrac19 + 4\tfrac{1}{27} + 8\tfrac{1}{81} + \cdots$

The general term is $T_n = 2^{n-1} + \left(\frac13\right)^n$. Find an expression for the sum of the first $n$ terms.
questions.answer:
Sum the two geometric series separately:
$$S_n = \frac{2^n - 1}{2 - 1} + \frac{\frac13\left(1 - \left(\frac13\right)^n\right)}{1 - \frac13} = 2^n - 1 + \frac12\left(1 - 3^{-n}\right) = 2^n - \frac12 - \frac{1}{2 \cdot 3^n}.$$

questions.question:
The decibel level of a sound is given by the formula
$$L = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I}{10^{-12}}\right),$$
where $L$ is the sound level in decibels and $I$ is the intensity of the sound in watts per square metre.

A chocolate making machine produces a sound with intensity $2.5 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{W/m}^2$. Calculate the sound level of the machine to 4 decimal places.

The decibel level of a sound is given by the formula
$$L = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I}{10^{-12}}\right),$$
where $L$ is the sound level in decibels and $I$ is the intensity of the sound in watts per square metre.

A chocolate making machine produces a sound with intensity $2.5 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{W/m}^2$. A nearby industrial coffee grinder produces a sound that is 20 decibels louder than the chocolate making machine. What is the percentage increase in sound intensity produced by the coffee grinder compared to the chocolate making machine? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
questions.answer:
Let the machine and grinder have intensities $I_1$ and $I_2$. Then
$$L_2 - L_1 = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I_2}{10^{-12}}\right) - 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I_1}{10^{-12}}\right) = 10\log_{10}\left(\frac{I_2}{I_1}\right) = 20.$$
So $\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{I_2}{I_1}\right) = 2$, i.e. $I_2 = 100I_1$: an increase of $\dfrac{100I_1 - I_1}{I_1} \times 100\% = 9900\%$.

questions.question:
Let $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1$.

Find any stationary points and determine their nature.

Let $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1$.

Find any points of inflection.
questions.answer: $f''(x) = 6x - 12 = 0 \implies x = 2$, $f(2) = 3$. $\;f''(1) = -6 < 0$ and $f''(3) = 6 > 0$, so the concavity changes: point of inflection at $(2, 3)$.

questions.question:
Let $f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1$.

$f$ has a local maximum at $(1, 5)$, a local minimum at $(3, 1)$ and a point of inflection at $(2, 3)$. Sketch the curve, showing all important features (you do not need to find the $x$-intercept).
questions.answer: $y$-intercept $(0, 1)$; maximum $(1, 5)$; inflection $(2, 3)$; minimum $(3, 1)$; $y \to \pm\infty$ as $x \to \pm\infty$.

questions.question: The $z$-scores on a test are normally distributed such that $P(-N < z < N) = p$ for some constants $N > 0$ and $0 < p < 1$. What is the value of $P(z < N)$?
questions.answer:
By symmetry, $P(z < 0) = \frac12$ and $P(0 < z < N) = \frac p2$, so
$$P(z < N) = \frac12 + \frac p2 = \frac{1 + p}{2}.$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows the graphs of the curves $y = \sec^2 x$ and $y = 2\tan^2 x$ for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

State the periods of each of the two curves.
questions.answer: Both curves have period $\pi$ (e.g. $\sec^2(x + \pi) = \sec^2 x$ and $\tan(x + \pi) = \tan x$).

questions.question:
The diagram shows the graphs of the curves $y = \sec^2 x$ and $y = 2\tan^2 x$ for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$.

Show that the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection of the two curves are solutions of the equation $\tan^2 x = 1$, and solve this equation for $\frac\pi2 \le x \le \frac{3\pi}{2}$.
questions.answer:
$$2\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x \implies \tan^2 x = 1 \implies \tan x = \pm1.$$
For $\frac\pi2 < x < \frac{3\pi}{2}$ (where $\tan x$ is defined): $x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ or $x = \dfrac{5\pi}{4}$.

questions.question: By using the trapezoidal rule with 4 subintervals, estimate the area under the curve for $\displaystyle\int_0^4\ln(x + 1)\,dx$.
questions.answer:
$h = 1$, function values at $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$: $\ln 1, \ln 2, \ln 3, \ln 4, \ln 5$.
$$\int_0^4\ln(x+1)\,dx \approx \frac12\left[\ln 1 + 2(\ln 2 + \ln 3 + \ln 4) + \ln 5\right] = \ln 24 + \tfrac12\ln 5 \approx 3.98.$$

questions.question: Let the equation of a curve be $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{e^x + 1}$. Find the equation of the normal to the curve at the point where $x = 1$, in general form.
questions.answer:
By the quotient rule:
$$f'(x) = \frac{(e^x + 1) - xe^x}{(e^x + 1)^2}, \qquad f'(1) = \frac{e + 1 - e}{(e + 1)^2} = \frac{1}{(e + 1)^2}.$$
So the normal has gradient $-(e + 1)^2$, and $f(1) = \dfrac{1}{e + 1}$:
$$y - \frac{1}{e+1} = -(e+1)^2(x - 1).$$
Multiplying by $(e + 1)$ and rearranging (no fractional coefficients):
$$(e+1)^3x + (e+1)y - (e+1)^3 - 1 = 0.$$

questions.question:
A car travels at 40 km/h on a circular curve whose radius is 500 m.

Find the distance, $l$ km, that the car travels in one minute.
questions.answer: $l = 40 \times \dfrac{1}{60} = \dfrac23$ km.

questions.question:
A car travels at 40 km/h on a circular curve whose radius is 500 m.

Calculate the size of the angle $\theta$ through which the car turns in 2 minutes. Give your answer to the nearest degree.
questions.answer:
In 2 minutes the car travels $\frac43$ km $= \frac{4000}{3}$ m. Using $l = r\theta$:
$$\theta = \frac{4000/3}{500} = \frac83 \text{ radians} = \frac83 \times \frac{180^\circ}{\pi} \approx 153^\circ.$$

questions.question: Differentiate $f(x) = \ln\left(\tan^2 x\right)$ and simplify your answer in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$.
questions.answer:
$f(x) = \ln\left(\sin^2 x\right) - \ln\left(\cos^2 x\right)$, so
$$f'(x) = \frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\sin^2 x} + \frac{2\cos x\sin x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{2\cos x}{\sin x} + \frac{2\sin x}{\cos x} = \frac{2\left(\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x\right)}{\sin x\cos x} = \frac{2}{\sin x\cos x}.$$

questions.question:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} e^{-\frac12x}, & 0 \le x \le k \\ 0, & \text{for all other values of } x. \end{cases}$$

Find the exact value of $k$.
questions.answer: $$\int_0^k e^{-x/2}\,dx = \Big[-2e^{-x/2}\Big]_0^k = 2\left(1 - e^{-k/2}\right) = 1 \implies e^{-k/2} = \frac12 \implies k = 2\ln 2.$$

questions.question:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} e^{-\frac12x}, & 0 \le x \le k \\ 0, & \text{for all other values of } x. \end{cases}$$

Given $k = 2\ln 2$, write the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ of $X$ for $-\infty < x < \infty$.
questions.answer: $$F(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 0 \\ 2\left(1 - e^{-x/2}\right), & 0 \le x \le 2\ln 2 \\ 1, & x > 2\ln 2. \end{cases}$$

questions.question:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} e^{-\frac12x}, & 0 \le x \le k \\ 0, & \text{for all other values of } x. \end{cases}$$

Given $k = 2\ln 2$ and $F(x) = 2\left(1 - e^{-x/2}\right)$ for $0 \le x \le k$, write the simplest exact form of the median of $X$.
questions.answer: $$2\left(1 - e^{-m/2}\right) = \frac12 \implies e^{-m/2} = \frac34 \implies m = 2\ln\frac43.$$

questions.question:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} e^{-\frac12x}, & 0 \le x \le k \\ 0, & \text{for all other values of } x. \end{cases}$$

The median of $X$ is $2\ln\frac43 \approx 0.575$. Let $X$ be the duration, in seconds, it takes for a student card to be registered by the school scanner. In words, interpret the value of the median in this context.
questions.answer: Half (50%) of student cards are registered in less than $2\ln\frac43 \approx 0.575$ seconds, and half take longer.

questions.question:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} e^{-\frac12x}, & 0 \le x \le k \\ 0, & \text{for all other values of } x. \end{cases}$$

Given $k = 2\ln 2$ and $F(x) = 2\left(1 - e^{-x/2}\right)$ for $0 \le x \le k$: given that $3P(X < c) = 2P(X > c)$, evaluate $c$ to 3 decimal places.
questions.answer:
$3P(X < c) = 2\left(1 - P(X < c)\right) \implies P(X < c) = 0.4$:
$$2\left(1 - e^{-c/2}\right) = 0.4 \implies e^{-c/2} = 0.8 \implies c = 2\ln 1.25 \approx 0.446.$$

questions.question: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{-6x^2}{\left(x^3 + 2\right)^2}\,dx$.
questions.answer:
Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^3 + 2\right) = 3x^2$:
$$\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{-6x^2}{\left(x^3 + 2\right)^2}\,dx = \left[\frac{2}{x^3 + 2}\right]_{-1}^{1} = \frac23 - 2 = -\frac43.$$

questions.question: Solve the equation $1 + 4 + 7 + \cdots + x = 925$.
questions.answer:
Arithmetic series with $a = 1$, $d = 3$:
$$\frac n2\left[2 + 3(n - 1)\right] = 925 \implies 3n^2 - n - 1850 = 0 \implies (n - 25)(3n + 74) = 0 \implies n = 25.$$
So $x = 1 + 24 \times 3 = 73$.

questions.question:
A right circular cone has height $H$ and a base of radius $R$. A square prism is inscribed in the cone so that the base of the prism is on the cone's base. The prism has height $h$ and a square base of side length $x$. The cross-section through the cone's axis (parallel to a side of the square) is shown.

By using similar triangles, show that $x = 2R\left(1 - \dfrac hH\right)$.
questions.answer:
In the cross-section, the top edge of the prism (half-width $\frac x2$, at height $h$) touches the cone. The small triangle above it is similar to the whole triangle (half-width $R$, height $H$):
$$\frac{x/2}{R} = \frac{H - h}{H} \implies x = 2R\left(1 - \frac hH\right).$$

questions.question:
A right circular cone has height $H$ and a base of radius $R$. A square prism is inscribed in the cone so that the base of the prism is on the cone's base. The prism has height $h$ and a square base of side length $x$. The cross-section through the cone's axis (parallel to a side of the square) is shown.

Given $x = 2R\left(1 - \dfrac hH\right)$, determine the height of the prism, in terms of $H$, that will maximise the volume of the prism.
questions.answer:
$$V = x^2h = 4R^2h\left(1 - \frac hH\right)^2, \quad 0 < h < H.$$
$$\frac{dV}{dh} = 4R^2\left[\left(1 - \frac hH\right)^2 - \frac{2h}{H}\left(1 - \frac hH\right)\right] = 4R^2\left(1 - \frac hH\right)\left(1 - \frac{3h}{H}\right) = 0 \implies h = \frac H3 \quad (h \ne H).$$
For $h$ just below $\frac H3$, $\frac{dV}{dh} > 0$; just above, $\frac{dV}{dh} < 0$: a maximum. The volume is greatest when $h = \dfrac H3$.

questions.question: Sketch the graph of $y = -2\cos(2\pi x)$ for $-1 \le x \le 1.5$ and show all important features.

A venetian blind consists of twenty slats, each 2.5 mm thick. When the blind is down, the gap between the top slat and the top of the blind is 27 mm, and the gap between adjacent slats is also 27 mm. When the blind is up, all the slats are stacked at the top with no gaps.

Show that when the blind is raised, the bottom slat rises 540 mm.
questions.answer: When the blind is raised, every gap disappears and nothing else changes. Above the bottom (20th) slat there are 20 gaps of 27 mm (the top gap and 19 gaps between slats), so it rises $20 \times 27 = 540$ mm.

questions.question:
A venetian blind consists of twenty slats, each 2.5 mm thick. When the blind is down, the gap between the top slat and the top of the blind is 27 mm, and the gap between adjacent slats is also 27 mm. When the blind is up, all the slats are stacked at the top with no gaps.

How far does the 19th slat rise?
questions.answer: Above the 19th slat there are 19 gaps: it rises $19 \times 27 = 513$ mm.

questions.question:
A venetian blind consists of twenty slats, each 2.5 mm thick. When the blind is down, the gap between the top slat and the top of the blind is 27 mm, and the gap between adjacent slats is also 27 mm. When the blind is up, all the slats are stacked at the top with no gaps.

Explain briefly why the distances the slats rise form an arithmetic sequence.
questions.answer: The $n$th slat has $n$ gaps above it, so it rises $27n$ mm. Each slat rises 27 mm more than the one above it — a constant difference — so the distances $27, 54, 81, \ldots, 540$ form an arithmetic sequence.

On the same set of axes, sketch the graph of $g(x) = -2\sqrt{x - 1} + 3$.
questions.answer: The curve starts at $(1, 3)$ and decreases; $x$-intercept where $\sqrt{x - 1} = \frac32$, i.e. $\left(\frac{13}{4}, 0\right)$; it passes through $(5, -1)$ and $(10, -3)$.

questions.question:
The graph of $f(x) = \sqrt x$ is given, and $g(x) = -2\sqrt{x - 1} + 3$.

Describe the sequence of transformations applied to $f(x)$ to obtain $g(x)$.
questions.answer: For example: translate **1 unit right**; dilate **vertically by a factor of 2**; **reflect in the $x$-axis**; then translate **3 units up**. (The dilation and reflection must come before the upward translation.)

questions.question:
The graph of $f(x) = \sqrt x$ is given, and $g(x) = -2\sqrt{x - 1} + 3$.

$g$ starts at $(1, 3)$ and crosses the $x$-axis at $x = \frac{13}{4}$. Find the area enclosed between the curve $y = g(x)$, the line $y = 4 - x$ and the $x$-axis, considering only the region that lies above the $x$-axis.
questions.answer:
The line $y = 4 - x$ also passes through $(1, 3)$ and meets the $x$-axis at $x = 4$. The region lies between the curve and the line above the $x$-axis, so
$$A = \underbrace{\tfrac12 \times 3 \times 3}_{\text{triangle under the line, } 1 \le x \le 4} - \int_1^{13/4}\left(3 - 2\sqrt{x - 1}\right)dx.$$
$$\int_1^{13/4}\left(3 - 2\sqrt{x - 1}\right)dx = \left[3x - \tfrac43(x - 1)^{3/2}\right]_1^{13/4} = \frac{27}{4} - \frac43 \times \frac{27}{8} = \frac94.$$
$$A = \frac92 - \frac94 = \frac94 \text{ square units}.$$

questions.question:
The hours of daylight in Sydney can be modelled by
$$y(t) = 2.24\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} + 1.34\right) + 12.19,$$
where $y$ is the number of hours of daylight and $t$ is the month of the year ($t = 1$ represents 1 January; ignore leap years).

In this model, what is the maximum number of daylight hours in one day?

The hours of daylight in Sydney can be modelled by
$$y(t) = 2.24\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} + 1.34\right) + 12.19,$$
where $y$ is the number of hours of daylight and $t$ is the month of the year ($t = 1$ represents 1 January; ignore leap years).

Find the month that has the longest day in terms of number of hours of daylight.
questions.answer:
Maximum when $\dfrac{\pi t}{6} + 1.34 = \dfrac{5\pi}{2}$ (the first such value with $t \ge 1$):
$$t = \frac6\pi\left(\frac{5\pi}{2} - 1.34\right) \approx 12.44,$$
so the longest day is in **December**.

questions.question:
The hours of daylight in Sydney can be modelled by
$$y(t) = 2.24\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} + 1.34\right) + 12.19,$$
where $y$ is the number of hours of daylight and $t$ is the month of the year ($t = 1$ represents 1 January; ignore leap years).

A scientist needs at least 13 hours of daylight each day for an experiment. Between which dates should they be looking to run the experiment?
questions.answer:
$$2.24\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} + 1.34\right) + 12.19 = 13 \implies \sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} + 1.34\right) = \frac{0.81}{2.24} = 0.3616\ldots$$
$$\frac{\pi t}{6} + 1.34 = 2.7717\ldots \text{ or } 6.6531\ldots \implies t \approx 2.734 \text{ or } t \approx 10.147.$$
Daylight exceeds 13 hours from $t \approx 10.15$ to $t \approx 12 + 2.73$, i.e. from about **4–5 October** until about **20 February**.

questions.question: What is the period of the function $f(x) = 2\cot(3x)$?
questions.answer: $\cot x$ has period $\pi$, so $\cot 3x$ has period $\dfrac\pi3$. **(A)**

questions.question: For a function $f(x)$, what type of dilation is required to sketch $y = f(4x)$?
questions.answer: Replacing $x$ by $4x = \dfrac{x}{1/4}$ dilates horizontally by a factor of $\frac14$. **(B)**

Horizontal dilation by a factor of $\frac14$

questions.question: Which of the following are the asymptote(s) of the graph of $y = \log(x - 1) + 2$?
questions.answer: $y = \log x$ has only the vertical asymptote $x = 0$; shifting right 1 and up 2 gives the single asymptote $x = 1$. **(B)**

questions.question: What is the solution of $3^x = 5$?
questions.answer: Take logs: $x\log 3 = \log 5 \implies x = \dfrac{\log 5}{\log 3}$. **(C)**

questions.question: Which of the following is the domain of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^2 - 4}}$?
questions.answer: Need $x^2 - 4 > 0$ (positive, since it is under a root in the denominator): $x < -2$ or $x > 2$. **(D)**

questions.question: Which of the following represents the range of the function $f(x) = -x^2 - 2x - 3$ for $x \in (-2, 1]$?
questions.answer: $f(x) = -(x + 1)^2 - 2$: maximum $-2$ at $x = -1$ (inside the interval). At the ends: $f(1) = -6$ (included) and $f(-2) = -3$ (excluded, but $-3$ is reached elsewhere). Range $[-6, -2]$. **(B)**

questions.question: From the graph of $y = f(x)$, which has a maximum turning point at $x = -2$ and a minimum turning point at $x = 2$, when is $f'(x)$ negative?
questions.answer: $f'(x) < 0$ where the curve is decreasing: strictly between the turning points, $-2 < x < 2$. **(B)**

questions.question: Find all the values of $k$ such that the equation $x^2 + (4k + 3)x + \left(4k^2 - \dfrac94\right) = 0$ has two real solutions for $x$, where one of the solutions is positive and the other is negative.
questions.answer: Roots of opposite sign means the product of roots is negative: $4k^2 - \frac94 < 0 \implies k^2 < \frac{9}{16} \implies -\frac34 < k < \frac34$. (Then $\Delta = b^2 - 4ac > 0$ automatically, since $ac < 0$.) **(C)**

questions.question: Evaluate $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 2}\frac{2 - x}{1 - \sqrt{x - 1}}$.
questions.answer:
Multiply top and bottom by $1 + \sqrt{x - 1}$:
$$\frac{(2 - x)\left(1 + \sqrt{x - 1}\right)}{1 - (x - 1)} = \frac{(2 - x)\left(1 + \sqrt{x - 1}\right)}{2 - x} = 1 + \sqrt{x - 1} \to 2.$$ **(C)**

questions.question:
Using the table below, what is the maximum possible value for $E(X)$?

| $x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X = x)$ | $k^2$ | $3k$ | $k$ | $-k^2 - 4k + 1$ |
questions.answer:
The probabilities always sum to 1; each must be non-negative, so $k \ge 0$ and $-k^2 - 4k + 1 \ge 0$, i.e. $0 \le k \le \sqrt5 - 2$.
$$E(X) = -k^2 + k + 2\left(-k^2 - 4k + 1\right) = -3k^2 - 7k + 2,$$
which is decreasing for $k \ge 0$, so the maximum is $E(X) = 2$ at $k = 0$. **(C)**

questions.question:
Solve for $x$:
$$2\ln(x) - \ln(x + 3) = \ln\left(\frac12\right)$$
questions.answer:
$$\ln\frac{x^2}{x + 3} = \ln\frac12 \implies 2x^2 = x + 3 \implies (2x - 3)(x + 1) = 0.$$
$x = \frac32$ or $x = -1$; since $\ln x$ needs $x > 0$, $x = \dfrac32$.

questions.question:
Hence or otherwise, find the value of $a$, where $a > 0$, such that
$$\int_{-\frac34}^{a}\left(2|2x + 1| - 1\right)dx = 0.$$
questions.answer:
$y = 2|2x + 1| - 1$ is a V with vertex $\left(-\frac12, -1\right)$, crossing the $x$-axis at $x = -\frac34$ and $x = -\frac14$.

From $-\frac34$ to $-\frac12$ the graph is a triangle below the axis of area $\frac12 \times \frac14 \times 1 = \frac18$, so $\displaystyle\int_{-3/4}^{-1/2} = -\frac18$. For $x \ge -\frac12$ the integrand is $4x + 1$, and $\displaystyle\int_{-1/2}^{0}(4x + 1)\,dx = \Big[2x^2 + x\Big]_{-1/2}^{0} = 0$, so $\displaystyle\int_{-3/4}^{0} = -\frac18$.

For $a > 0$ we need $\displaystyle\int_0^a(4x + 1)\,dx = \frac18$:
$$2a^2 + a = \frac18 \implies 16a^2 + 8a - 1 = 0 \implies a = \frac{-8 + \sqrt{128}}{32} = \frac{\sqrt2 - 1}{4}.$$

questions.question:
Initially there are 250 litres of water in a tank. Water starts to flow into the tank. The rate of increase of the volume of water in litres is given by
$$\frac{dV}{dt} = 250 - 7.5t$$
where $t$ is the time in hours. Find the volume of water in the tank (correct to the nearest litre) when $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 0$.
questions.answer:
$V = 250t - 3.75t^2 + C$, and $V(0) = 250 \implies C = 250$.

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 0 \implies t = \dfrac{100}{3}$:
$$V = 250\left(\frac{100}{3}\right) - 3.75\left(\frac{100}{3}\right)^2 + 250 = 4416.6\ldots \approx 4417 \text{ litres}.$$

questions.question:
Consider the function $f(x) = xe^x$.

Find the coordinates of the stationary point(s) and determine their nature, find the coordinates of the point(s) of inflection, and sketch the curve of $f(x)$, showing all key features.
questions.answer:
$f'(x) = e^x + xe^x = e^x(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = -1$, $f(-1) = -\frac1e$. $f'$ changes from negative to positive, so $\left(-1, -\frac1e\right)$ is a **local minimum**.

$f''(x) = e^x(x + 2) = 0 \implies x = -2$, $f(-2) = -\frac{2}{e^2}$. $f''$ changes sign, so $\left(-2, -\frac{2}{e^2}\right)$ is a **point of inflection**.

The curve passes through the origin, and $f(x) \to 0^-$ as $x \to -\infty$ (horizontal asymptote $y = 0$).

questions.question:
Consider the function $f(x) = xe^x$.

$y = xe^x$ has a local minimum at $\left(-1, -\frac1e\right)$, passes through the origin and approaches $0$ from below as $x \to -\infty$. Hence or otherwise, find the value(s) of $k$, where $k$ is a real number, for which the equation $xe^x = k$ has 2 solutions.
questions.answer: A horizontal line $y = k$ meets the curve twice only between the minimum and the asymptote: $-\dfrac1e < k < 0$.

questions.question:
A random variable $X$ has this probability distribution:

| $x$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X = x)$ | 0.2 | 0.1 | 0.25 | 0.3 | 0.15 |

Find $P(X \ge 2 \mid X < 4)$.

A random variable $X$ has this probability distribution:

| $x$ | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(X = x)$ | 0.2 | 0.1 | 0.25 | 0.3 | 0.15 |

Find the variance of $X$, $\operatorname{Var}(X)$.

Joe plays soccer, a sport where a team can win, lose or draw. Joe is prone to injury, and misses 20% of his team's games. When Joe plays, his team has a 77% chance of winning and a 10% chance of losing. When Joe does not play, his team has a 53% chance of winning and a 25% chance of losing.

Calculate the probability that Joe's team loses any given game.

Joe plays soccer, a sport where a team can win, lose or draw. Joe is prone to injury, and misses 20% of his team's games. When Joe plays, his team has a 77% chance of winning and a 10% chance of losing. When Joe does not play, his team has a 53% chance of winning and a 25% chance of losing.

$P(\text{lose}) = 0.13$. Given that Joe's team does not lose in a particular match, what is the probability that Joe played in that match?

Prove the following identity:
$$\frac{\cos\theta}{\cos\left(\frac\pi2 - \theta\right)}\left(1 + \tan^2\theta\right) + \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\left(1 + \tan^2\left(\frac\pi2 - \theta\right)\right) = 2\operatorname{cosec}\theta\sec\theta$$
questions.answer:
Use $\cos\left(\frac\pi2 - \theta\right) = \sin\theta$, $1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta$ and $1 + \tan^2\left(\frac\pi2 - \theta\right) = 1 + \cot^2\theta = \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\text{LHS} &= \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} \cdot \frac{1}{\cos^2\theta} + \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} \cdot \frac{1}{\sin^2\theta} = \frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} + \frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\\
&= \frac{2}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = 2\operatorname{cosec}\theta\sec\theta = \text{RHS}.
\end{aligned}$$

questions.question:
The number of concert tickets sold, $N$, is given by $N = 1000 \times 1.6^{kt}$, where $t$ is the number of weeks after being available for sale, and $k$ is a constant. Initially, 1000 tickets were sold, and after 2 weeks, the total number of tickets sold had doubled.

Calculate the value of $k$, leaving your answer in exact form.
questions.answer: $1000 \times 1.6^{2k} = 2000 \implies 2k\ln 1.6 = \ln 2 \implies k = \dfrac{\ln 2}{2\ln 1.6}$.

questions.question:
The number of concert tickets sold, $N$, is given by $N = 1000 \times 1.6^{kt}$, where $t$ is the number of weeks after being available for sale, and $k$ is a constant. Initially, 1000 tickets were sold, and after 2 weeks, the total number of tickets sold had doubled.

$k = \dfrac{\ln 2}{2\ln 1.6}$. At what rate was the number of tickets sold increasing after 4 weeks? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{dN}{dt} = 1000k\ln(1.6) \times 1.6^{kt}$. With $k\ln 1.6 = \frac{\ln 2}{2}$ and $1.6^{4k} = 2^2 = 4$:
$$\frac{dN}{dt} = 1000 \times \frac{\ln 2}{2} \times 4 = 2000\ln 2 \approx 1386 \text{ tickets per week}.$$

questions.question:
A fisherman's boat is trying to reach the open sea, however, it is heavily affected by the ocean tides. To reach the open sea, the boat must cross a sandbar which requires the water to be at least 4 metres deep. On a particular day, high tide occurred at midnight, and the depth, $D$, of water over the sandbar on the ensuing day is given by
$$D = 2\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}t\right) + 3,$$
where $t$ is the number of hours after midnight.

Sketch the graph of $D = 2\cos\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{25}t\right) + 3$ for $0 \le t \le 25$, showing all key features.
questions.answer: Period $\dfrac{2\pi}{4\pi/25} = \dfrac{25}{2}$ hours, amplitude 2, centre line $D = 3$. Maxima $D = 5$ at $t = 0, \frac{25}{2}, 25$; minima $D = 1$ at $t = \frac{25}{4}, \frac{75}{4}$.

questions.question:
A fisherman's boat is trying to reach the open sea, however, it is heavily affected by the ocean tides. To reach the open sea, the boat must cross a sandbar which requires the water to be at least 4 metres deep. On a particular day, high tide occurred at midnight, and the depth, $D$, of water over the sandbar on the ensuing day is given by
$$D = 2\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}t\right) + 3,$$
where $t$ is the number of hours after midnight.

Find the times when the fisherman would not be able to cross the sandbar in his boat.
questions.answer:
$D = 4 \implies \cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{25}t\right) = \frac12$. With $0 \le \frac{4\pi}{25}t \le 4\pi$:
$$\frac{4\pi}{25}t = \frac\pi3, \frac{5\pi}{3}, \frac{7\pi}{3}, \frac{11\pi}{3} \implies t = \frac{25}{12}, \frac{125}{12}, \frac{175}{12}, \frac{275}{12}.$$
$D < 4$ for $\dfrac{25}{12} < t < \dfrac{125}{12}$ and $\dfrac{175}{12} < t < \dfrac{275}{12}$, i.e. from 2:05 am to 10:25 am and from 2:35 pm to 8:55 pm.

questions.question: Show that $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{1}{1 + e^{-x}}\,dx = 1$.
questions.answer:
Multiply top and bottom by $e^x$:
$$\int_{-1}^1\frac{e^x}{e^x + 1}\,dx = \Big[\ln\left(1 + e^x\right)\Big]_{-1}^1 = \ln\frac{1 + e}{1 + e^{-1}} = \ln\frac{e(1 + e)}{e + 1} = \ln e = 1.$$

questions.question:
It is known that $T_1 = 1 + \cos A$, $T_2 = \dfrac12$ and $T_3 = 1 - \cos A$ form the first three consecutive terms of a geometric sequence, with $T_1 > T_2 > T_3$.

Find the value of $A$, given $\angle A$ is an angle within a triangle.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \dfrac{T_3}{T_2} \implies \frac14 = (1 + \cos A)(1 - \cos A) = 1 - \cos^2A \implies \cos A = \pm\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, so $A = \frac\pi6$ or $\frac{5\pi}{6}$ (as $0 < A < \pi$).

$T_1 > T_2$ needs $1 + \cos A > \frac12$, which rules out $A = \frac{5\pi}{6}$ ($1 - \frac{\sqrt3}{2} \approx 0.13$). So $A = \dfrac\pi6$.

questions.question:
It is known that $T_1 = 1 + \cos A$, $T_2 = \dfrac12$ and $T_3 = 1 - \cos A$ form the first three consecutive terms of a geometric sequence, with $T_1 > T_2 > T_3$.

Using $A = \dfrac\pi6$, show that the series $(1 + \cos A) + \dfrac12 + (1 - \cos A) + \cdots$ has a limiting sum.
questions.answer:
$$r = \frac{T_2}{T_1} = \frac{\frac12}{1 + \frac{\sqrt3}{2}} = \frac{1}{2 + \sqrt3} \approx 0.268.$$
Since $|r| < 1$, the limiting sum exists.

questions.question: If $y^2 = (2m - y)(2n - y)$, show that $\dfrac1m, \dfrac1y, \dfrac1n$ (in this order) form the terms of an arithmetic sequence.
questions.answer:
Expand: $y^2 = 4mn - 2my - 2ny + y^2 \implies y = \dfrac{2mn}{m + n}$, so $\dfrac1y = \dfrac{m + n}{2mn}$.
$$\frac1y - \frac1m = \frac{m + n - 2n}{2mn} = \frac{m - n}{2mn}, \qquad \frac1n - \frac1y = \frac{2m - m - n}{2mn} = \frac{m - n}{2mn}.$$
The common difference is the same, so the three terms form an arithmetic sequence.

questions.question:
A tall pole $OT$ is held in place vertically by ropes anchored by two pegs in the ground 10 metres apart at $A$ and $B$ as shown. $A$ is due west of $O$, and $B$ is at a bearing of 240°T from $O$. The rope connecting the top of the pole $T$ to the peg at $A$ is $3\sqrt3$ metres long and makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the ground. The rope from $T$ to $B$ has length $\ell$.

Show that $OB = \dfrac{9 + 11\sqrt{13}}{4}$ metres.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle AOT$: $AO = 3\sqrt3\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}$. $\;\angle AOB = 270^\circ - 240^\circ = 30^\circ$.

Cosine rule in $\triangle AOB$:
$$10^2 = \frac{27}{4} + OB^2 - 2\left(\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)OB\cos 30^\circ = \frac{27}{4} + OB^2 - \frac92OB$$
$$\implies 4OB^2 - 18OB - 373 = 0 \implies OB = \frac{18 \pm \sqrt{6292}}{8} = \frac{9 \pm 11\sqrt{13}}{4}.$$
Since $OB > 0$, $OB = \dfrac{9 + 11\sqrt{13}}{4}$ m.

questions.question:
A tall pole $OT$ is held in place vertically by ropes anchored by two pegs in the ground 10 metres apart at $A$ and $B$ as shown. $A$ is due west of $O$, and $B$ is at a bearing of 240°T from $O$. The rope connecting the top of the pole $T$ to the peg at $A$ is $3\sqrt3$ metres long and makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the ground. The rope from $T$ to $B$ has length $\ell$.

Given $OB = \dfrac{9 + 11\sqrt{13}}{4}$ metres, find the length of the rope, $\ell$, connecting $T$ and $B$. Give your answer to the nearest metre.
questions.answer:
$OT = 3\sqrt3\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac92$. $\triangle TOB$ is right-angled at $O$:
$$\ell = \sqrt{\left(\frac{9 + 11\sqrt{13}}{4}\right)^2 + \left(\frac92\right)^2} \approx 12.97 \approx 13\ \text{m}.$$

questions.question: The line $y = mx$ is a tangent to the curve $y = \ln(kx)$, where $k > 0$. Find the value of $m$, in terms of $k$.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{k}{kx} = \dfrac1x$, so at the point of contact $m = \dfrac1x$. The point is on both graphs:
$$mx = \ln(kx) \implies 1 = \ln(kx) \implies x = \frac ek.$$
So $m = \dfrac{k}{e}$.

Using the trapezoidal rule with 4 function values, find the approximate shaded area in exact form.
questions.answer:
Function values at $x = 1, 3, 5, 7$ ($h = 2$):
$$A \approx \frac22\left[\ln 1 + 2(\ln 3 + \ln 5) + \ln 7\right] = 2\ln 3 + 2\ln 5 + \ln 7 \;(= \ln 1575).$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows the graph of $y = \ln x$. The region bounded by the graph, the $x$-axis and the line $x = 7$ has been shaded.

Find $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\ln x)$.
questions.answer: By the product rule: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\ln x) = 1 \cdot \ln x + x \cdot \dfrac1x = \ln x + 1$.

questions.question:
The diagram shows the graph of $y = \ln x$. The region bounded by the graph, the $x$-axis and the line $x = 7$ has been shaded.

Given that $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\ln x) = \ln x + 1$, find $\displaystyle\int_1^7 \ln x\,dx$.
questions.answer:
From the derivative, $\displaystyle\int(\ln x + 1)\,dx = x\ln x + C$, so $\displaystyle\int\ln x\,dx = x\ln x - x + C$.
$$\int_1^7\ln x\,dx = \Big[x\ln x - x\Big]_1^7 = (7\ln 7 - 7) - (0 - 1) = 7\ln 7 - 6.$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows the graph of $y = \ln x$. The region bounded by the graph, the $x$-axis and the line $x = 7$ has been shaded.

The trapezoidal rule with 4 function values gives the approximation $2(\ln 3 + \ln 5) + \ln 7$ for the shaded area, and its exact value is $7\ln 7 - 6$. Deduce that $\ln 7 \approx \frac13(\ln 3 + \ln 5) + 1$.
questions.answer: $$7\ln 7 - 6 \approx 2(\ln 3 + \ln 5) + \ln 7 \implies 6\ln 7 \approx 2(\ln 3 + \ln 5) + 6 \implies \ln 7 \approx \frac13(\ln 3 + \ln 5) + 1.$$

questions.question:
The acceleration of a particle moving along the $x$-axis is given by $\ddot x = 4\sin 2t$, where $x$ is the displacement of the particle from the origin in metres, and $t$ is the time in seconds. Initially, the particle is at the origin moving to the left at 1 metre per second.

Show that the velocity of the particle is given by $\dot x = 1 - 2\cos 2t$.
questions.answer: $\dot x = \displaystyle\int 4\sin 2t\,dt = -2\cos 2t + C$. At $t = 0$, $\dot x = -1$ (moving left): $-1 = -2 + C \implies C = 1$. So $\dot x = 1 - 2\cos 2t$.

questions.question:
The acceleration of a particle moving along the $x$-axis is given by $\ddot x = 4\sin 2t$, where $x$ is the displacement of the particle from the origin in metres, and $t$ is the time in seconds. Initially, the particle is at the origin moving to the left at 1 metre per second.

The velocity is $\dot x = 1 - 2\cos 2t$. Find the time when the particle first comes to rest.
questions.answer: $1 - 2\cos 2t = 0 \implies \cos 2t = \frac12 \implies 2t = \frac\pi3 \implies t = \dfrac\pi6$ seconds.

questions.question:
The acceleration of a particle moving along the $x$-axis is given by $\ddot x = 4\sin 2t$, where $x$ is the displacement of the particle from the origin in metres, and $t$ is the time in seconds. Initially, the particle is at the origin moving to the left at 1 metre per second.

The velocity is $\dot x = 1 - 2\cos 2t$, and the particle first comes to rest at $t = \frac\pi6$. Find the distance travelled by the particle in the first $\dfrac\pi2$ seconds.
questions.answer:
$\dot x < 0$ on $\left(0, \frac\pi6\right)$ and $\dot x > 0$ on $\left(\frac\pi6, \frac\pi2\right]$.
$$\int_0^{\pi/6}(1 - 2\cos 2t)\,dt = \Big[t - \sin 2t\Big]_0^{\pi/6} = \frac\pi6 - \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\;(< 0), \qquad \int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/2}(1 - 2\cos 2t)\,dt = \frac\pi2 - \left(\frac\pi6 - \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right) = \frac\pi3 + \frac{\sqrt3}{2}.$$
$$\text{Distance} = \left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2} - \frac\pi6\right) + \left(\frac\pi3 + \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right) = \sqrt3 + \frac\pi6 \text{ metres}.$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows a rectangle $PQRS$ drawn in a sector $OAB$ with radius 5 metres, with $R$ and $S$ on $OA$, $Q$ on $OB$ and $P$ on the arc. It is given that $\angle AOB = \theta$, $OR = x$, $RS = y$ and $\tan\theta = 2$.

Show that the perimeter of the rectangle is given by $2x + 2\sqrt{25 - 4x^2}$.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle QOR$: $QR = x\tan\theta = 2x$, so $PS = 2x$. In right-angled $\triangle POS$:
$$(x + y)^2 + (2x)^2 = 5^2 \implies x + y = \sqrt{25 - 4x^2} \implies y = \sqrt{25 - 4x^2} - x.$$
Perimeter $= 2(2x) + 2y = 4x + 2\sqrt{25 - 4x^2} - 2x = 2x + 2\sqrt{25 - 4x^2}$.

questions.question:
The diagram shows a rectangle $PQRS$ drawn in a sector $OAB$ with radius 5 metres, with $R$ and $S$ on $OA$, $Q$ on $OB$ and $P$ on the arc. It is given that $\angle AOB = \theta$, $OR = x$, $RS = y$ and $\tan\theta = 2$.

The perimeter of the rectangle is $P = 2x + 2\sqrt{25 - 4x^2}$. Find the maximum perimeter of the rectangle. Leave your answer in exact form.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{dP}{dx} = 2 - \frac{8x}{\sqrt{25 - 4x^2}} = 0 \implies \sqrt{25 - 4x^2} = 4x \implies 25 = 20x^2 \implies x = \frac{\sqrt5}{2}.$$
$\dfrac{dP}{dx}$ changes from positive to negative there (e.g. $P'(1) > 0$, $P'(2) < 0$), so it is a maximum:
$$P_{\max} = \sqrt5 + 2 \times 4 \times \frac{\sqrt5}{2} = 5\sqrt5 \text{ metres}.$$

questions.question: What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to the line $y = 2x + 1$?
questions.answer: Perpendicular gradients multiply to $-1$: $m \times 2 = -1 \implies m = -\frac12$. **(D)**

questions.question: Which of the following is the natural domain of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x - 3}}$?
questions.answer: Need $x - 3 > 0$ (inside the root non-negative, and the denominator non-zero): $x > 3$. **(A)**

questions.question: Which of the following is the range of $y = 1 - e^x$?
questions.answer: $e^x$ takes every value in $(0, \infty)$, so $1 - e^x$ takes every value less than 1: $y < 1$. **(A)**

questions.question: How many solutions does the equation $x^2 = \cos x$ have?
questions.answer: Sketch $y = x^2$ and $y = \cos x$: they cross once for $x > 0$ (between $0$ and $1$) and, by symmetry, once for $x < 0$; for $|x| \ge 1$, $x^2 \ge 1 \ge \cos x$ with no further crossings. Two solutions. **(C)**

questions.question: The function $y = f(x)$ is dilated vertically by a factor of 3. Which of the following corresponds to the function of this transformation?
questions.answer: A vertical dilation by factor 3 replaces $y$ by $\frac y3$: $\frac y3 = f(x)$, i.e. $y = 3f(x)$. **(B)**

questions.question: A particle is moving along the $x$-axis. At a certain time, the particle's acceleration is opposite in direction to its velocity. Which of the following MUST be true at that time?
questions.answer: When $v$ and $a$ have opposite signs the particle is slowing down, so its speed is decreasing. (Velocity itself may be increasing, e.g. $v = -1$, $a = 2$, or decreasing, e.g. $v = 1$, $a = -2$.) **(B)**
options: The particle's speed at that time is increasing.
The particle's speed at that time is decreasing.
The particle's velocity at that time is increasing.
The particle's velocity at that time is decreasing.

questions.question: The velocity–time graph of a moving particle is shown: $v > 0$ for $0 < t < a$, $v < 0$ for $a < t < c$ (with minimum velocity at $t = b$), and $v > 0$ for $c < t \le d$. At what time does the particle reach its minimum displacement within the time frame $0 \le t \le d$?
questions.answer: The displacement decreases while $v < 0$, i.e. from $t = a$ to $t = c$, and increases after $t = c$. From the graph, the area below the axis is larger than the area above it before $t = a$, so the displacement is least at $t = c$. **(C)**

questions.question: Suppose $h(x) = [f(3x)]^2$. Which of the following is the correct expression for $h'(x)$?
questions.answer: Chain rule (twice): $h'(x) = 2f(3x) \cdot f'(3x) \cdot 3 = 6f'(3x)f(3x)$. **(D)**

questions.question: Which of the following is the solution to $x^2 \le x$?
questions.answer: $x^2 - x \le 0 \iff x(x - 1) \le 0 \iff 0 \le x \le 1$. **(A)**

questions.question: Which of the following definite integrals gives the largest value?
questions.answer: (A) $= e - e^{-1} \approx 2.35$. (B): $e^{x^2} \le 1 + (e - 1)x^2$ on $[-1, 1]$ (convexity in $x^2$), so (B) $\le \frac12\left(2 + \frac{2(e-1)}{3}\right) \approx 1.57$. (C) $= 0$ (odd function). (D) $= \frac\pi2 \approx 1.57$ (semicircle area). The largest is (A). **(A)**

questions.question: Solve $x - \dfrac6x = 1$.
questions.answer: Multiply by $x$ ($x \ne 0$): $x^2 - x - 6 = 0 \implies (x - 3)(x + 2) = 0 \implies x = 3$ or $x = -2$.

questions.question: Find the derivative of $y = 2x^3 + \dfrac1x$.
questions.answer: $y = 2x^3 + x^{-1} \implies \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 6x^2 - \dfrac{1}{x^2}$.

questions.question: Find the derivative of $y = 5e^{3x}$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 15e^{3x}$.

questions.question: Find the derivative of $y = \tan 2x$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\sec^2 2x$.

questions.question: Find the derivative of $y = \ln(3x - 1)$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{3x - 1}$.

questions.question: Find the equation of the tangent to $y = \sqrt{2x + 1}$ at $x = 4$. Give your answer in the form $ax + by + c = 0$, where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers and $a > 0$.
questions.answer:
At $x = 4$, $y = 3$. $\;\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac12(2x + 1)^{-1/2} \times 2 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2x + 1}} = \dfrac13$ at $x = 4$.
$$y - 3 = \frac13(x - 4) \implies 3y - 9 = x - 4 \implies x - 3y + 5 = 0.$$

questions.question:
Find the values of $x$ such that the following limiting sum exists:
$$1 + (1 - 2x) + (1 - 2x)^2 + (1 - 2x)^3 + \cdots$$
questions.answer:
Geometric series with $r = 1 - 2x$; a limiting sum exists when $|r| < 1$:
$$-1 < 1 - 2x < 1 \implies -2 < -2x < 0 \implies 0 < x < 1.$$

questions.question:
A team has a $\frac13$ chance of winning any given game. They play 3 games.

Find the probability of them winning at least one game.
questions.answer: $P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\text{lose all 3}) = 1 - \left(\frac23\right)^3 = \frac{19}{27}$.

questions.question:
A team has a $\frac13$ chance of winning any given game. They play 3 games.

Find the probability of them winning exactly one game.
questions.answer: The win can be in any of the 3 games: $P = 3 \times \frac13 \times \left(\frac23\right)^2 = \frac49$.

questions.question: Find the value of the arithmetic series $1 + 5 + 9 + \cdots + 2025$.

In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 5$ cm, $BC = x$ cm, $AC = 6$ cm and $\angle CAB = 60^\circ$.

Find the area of $\triangle ABC$ correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer: $A = \frac12 \times 5 \times 6 \times \sin 60^\circ = \frac{15\sqrt3}{2} \approx 12.99\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.question:
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 5$ cm, $BC = x$ cm, $AC = 6$ cm and $\angle CAB = 60^\circ$.

Find the exact value of $x$.
questions.answer: Cosine rule: $x^2 = 5^2 + 6^2 - 2(5)(6)\cos 60^\circ = 61 - 30 = 31 \implies x = \sqrt{31}$.

questions.question:
Consider $y = 2\sin 3t + 4$.

State its period.
questions.answer: Period $= \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

questions.question:
Consider $y = 2\sin 3t + 4$.

State its range.

Consider the curve $y = \dfrac{1}{27}x^3 - x + 2$.

Find the coordinates of its stationary points and determine their nature.

Consider the curve $y = \dfrac{1}{27}x^3 - x + 2$.

Find any points of inflection.
questions.answer: $y'' = \dfrac{2x}{9} = 0 \implies x = 0$, $y = 2$. $\;y''$ changes sign at $x = 0$ (negative to positive), so $(0, 2)$ is a point of inflection.

questions.question:
Consider the curve $y = \dfrac{1}{27}x^3 - x + 2$.

The curve has a maximum at $(-3, 4)$, a minimum at $(3, 0)$ and a point of inflection at $(0, 2)$. Given that $x = -6$ is an $x$-intercept, sketch the graph of the curve, clearly labelling stationary points, points of inflection and intercepts with the coordinate axes.
questions.answer: $x$-intercepts $(-6, 0)$ and $(3, 0)$ (the curve touches the axis at its minimum); $y$-intercept $(0, 2)$, which is also the point of inflection; maximum $(-3, 4)$.

questions.question: Find $\displaystyle\int\left(\frac{1}{x^2} - \cos 3x\right)dx$.
questions.answer: $$\int\left(x^{-2} - \cos 3x\right)dx = -\frac1x - \frac13\sin 3x + C.$$

Given $f'(x) = e^x(x + 2)$ and $f''(x) = e^x(x + 3)$, by identifying a pattern, write down an expression for the $n$th derivative of $f(x)$, where $n$ is a positive integer.
questions.answer: Each differentiation adds 1 inside the bracket: $f^{(n)}(x) = e^x(x + n + 1)$.

questions.question:
The region bounded by $y = \ln x$ and the $x$-axis between $x = 1$ and $x = 10$ is shaded in the diagram.

By using the trapezoidal rule with 4 function values, find an approximation for the area of the shaded region. Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
Function values at $x = 1, 4, 7, 10$ ($h = 3$):
$$A \approx \frac32\left[\ln 1 + 2(\ln 4 + \ln 7) + \ln 10\right] = \frac32\left[0 + 2(3.3322\ldots) + 2.3025\ldots\right] \approx 13.45.$$

questions.question:
The region bounded by $y = \ln x$ and the $x$-axis between $x = 1$ and $x = 10$ is shaded in the diagram.

By considering an appropriate region bounded by $y = \ln x$ and the $y$-axis, find the exact area of the shaded region.
questions.answer:
$y = \ln x \iff x = e^y$. The region between the curve and the $y$-axis, from $y = 0$ to $y = \ln 10$, has area
$$\int_0^{\ln 10} e^y\,dy = \Big[e^y\Big]_0^{\ln 10} = 10 - 1 = 9.$$
That region and the shaded region together make up the rectangle with vertices $(0,0)$, $(10,0)$, $(10,\ln 10)$, $(0,\ln 10)$, of area $10\ln 10$. So
$$\text{shaded area} = 10\ln 10 - 9 \text{ square units } (\approx 14.03).$$

questions.question: Find the area bounded between the graphs of $y = \sqrt{x - 1}$ and $y = x - 1$.
questions.answer:
Intersections: $\sqrt{x - 1} = x - 1 \implies x - 1 = 0$ or $1$, i.e. $x = 1, 2$. On $[1, 2]$, $\sqrt{x - 1} \ge x - 1$:
$$A = \int_1^2\left(\sqrt{x - 1} - (x - 1)\right)dx = \left[\tfrac23(x - 1)^{3/2} - \tfrac12(x - 1)^2\right]_1^2 = \frac23 - \frac12 = \frac16 \text{ square units}.$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows the graph of a parabola $y = f(x)$ whose vertex is at the origin (it is concave up). Let $k$ be some positive number.

State the coordinates of the vertex of $y = f(x) + k$ in terms of $k$.
questions.answer: The graph moves up $k$ units: vertex $(0, k)$.

questions.question:
The diagram shows the graph of a parabola $y = f(x)$ whose vertex is at the origin (it is concave up). Let $k$ be some positive number.

Write down the solution to $f(x) > f(x - k)$ in terms of $k$.
questions.answer:
$y = f(x - k)$ is $y = f(x)$ moved $k$ units right; the two parabolas cross halfway between their vertices, at $x = \frac k2$. To the right of that, $f(x)$ is higher. So $x > \dfrac k2$.

(For example, with $f(x) = ax^2$: $ax^2 > a(x - k)^2 \iff 2kx > k^2 \iff x > \frac k2$.)

questions.question:
The mass of a decaying radioactive substance, in kg, at time $t$ years is given by $M = 2e^{-kt}$, where $k$ is a positive constant.

State the initial mass of the radioactive substance.

The mass of a decaying radioactive substance, in kg, at time $t$ years is given by $M = 2e^{-kt}$, where $k$ is a positive constant.

Find the half-life of the radioactive substance. Give your answer as an exact value in terms of $k$.
questions.answer: $1 = 2e^{-kt} \implies e^{kt} = 2 \implies t = \dfrac{\ln 2}{k}$ years.

questions.question:
The mass of a decaying radioactive substance, in kg, at time $t$ years is given by $M = 2e^{-kt}$, where $k$ is a positive constant.

Find $\dfrac{dM}{dt}$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dM}{dt} = -2ke^{-kt}$.

questions.question:
The mass of a decaying radioactive substance, in kg, at time $t$ years is given by $M = 2e^{-kt}$, where $k$ is a positive constant.

$\dfrac{dM}{dt} = -2ke^{-kt}$. A biomaterial is also decaying simultaneously, but at every instant in time its rate of decay is twice as fast as the radioactive substance. Find an expression for the mass of the biomaterial, in terms of $k$ and $t$, given that its initial mass is 3 kg.
questions.answer:
Let $B$ be the biomaterial's mass. Its rate is twice the substance's rate:
$$\frac{dB}{dt} = 2 \times \left(-2ke^{-kt}\right) = -4ke^{-kt} \implies B = 4e^{-kt} + C.$$
$B(0) = 3 \implies 4 + C = 3 \implies C = -1$. So $B = 4e^{-kt} - 1$.

questions.question:
A particle is moving along the $x$-axis. Its velocity in metres per second, at time $t$ seconds, is given by
$$v = \frac{2}{t + 1} - 1.$$

Find the time at which the particle is stationary.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{2}{t + 1} = 1 \implies t = 1$ second.

questions.question:
A particle is moving along the $x$-axis. Its velocity in metres per second, at time $t$ seconds, is given by
$$v = \frac{2}{t + 1} - 1.$$

The particle is stationary at $t = 1$. Find the acceleration of the particle when it is stationary.
questions.answer: $a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = -\dfrac{2}{(t + 1)^2}$, so at $t = 1$: $a = -\dfrac12\ \text{m/s}^2$.
