$$x=\frac{2(12-\sqrt3)}{3\sqrt3}\times\frac{\sqrt3}{\sqrt3}=\frac{24\sqrt3-6}{9}=\frac{8\sqrt3-2}{3}$$

questions.question: A circle is defined by $x^2+2x+y^2+y-2=y+1$. Determine its centre and radius.
questions.answer:
$$x^2+2x+y^2=3\ \Rightarrow\ x^2+2x+1+y^2=4\ \Rightarrow\ (x+1)^2+y^2=4$$
Centre $(-1,0)$, radius $2$.

questions.question: Differentiate $y=\dfrac{2x}{3x^2+1}$.
Find $\displaystyle\int\sqrt[3]{4x+7}\,dx$.
questions.answer: $$\int(4x+7)^{\frac13}\,dx=\frac{(4x+7)^{\frac43}}{\frac43}\times\frac14+C=\frac{3(4x+7)^{\frac43}}{16}+C$$

questions.question:
The students in a school were surveyed on the number of hours of sleep they have per week. The results were normally distributed. The survey indicated that 95% of students had between 42 and 54 hours of sleep per week.

Determine the mean number of hours of sleep per week.
questions.answer: 95% of normally distributed data lies within two standard deviations of the mean, so 42 and 54 have $z$-scores $-2$ and $2$. The mean is midway: $\mu=\dfrac{42+54}{2}=48$ hours.

questions.question:
The students in a school were surveyed on the number of hours of sleep they have per week. The results were normally distributed. The survey indicated that 95% of students had between 42 and 54 hours of sleep per week.

What was the standard deviation?
questions.answer: There are 4 standard deviations between 42 and 54 hours, so $\sigma=\dfrac{54-42}{4}=3$ hours.

questions.question:
The students in a school were surveyed on the number of hours of sleep they have per week. The results were normally distributed. The survey indicated that 95% of students had between 42 and 54 hours of sleep per week.

What percentage of students would have indicated they had between 51 and 57 hours of sleep per week? (The mean is 48 hours and the standard deviation is 3 hours.)

Point $P(-1,-2)$ lies on $y=f(x)$. Point $P'$ is the image of point $P$ on the function $g(x)=2f(3x-1)$.

By clearly stating the transformations required to produce $g(x)$ from $f(x)$, show that the coordinates of point $P'$ are $(0,-4)$.
questions.answer:
| New function | Transformation | New point |
|---|---|---|
| $y=2f(x)$ | Vertical dilation, scale factor 2 | $(-1,\,-2\times2)=(-1,-4)$ |
| $y=2f(x-1)$ | Translation 1 unit right | $(-1+1,\,-4)=(0,-4)$ |
| $y=2f(3x-1)$ | Horizontal dilation, scale factor $\frac13$ | $(0\times\frac13,\,-4)=(0,-4)$ |

So $P'=(0,-4)$. (Check: $g(0)=2f(-1)=2(-2)=-4$.)

questions.question:
Ringo and Greg start at location $P$ and drive in different directions. Ringo drives at a speed of 70 km/h on a bearing of $285^\circ$, while Greg drives at a speed of 60 km/h on a bearing of $030^\circ$, as shown in the diagram.

Show that $\angle GPR=105^\circ$.
questions.answer:
Ringo's bearing $285^\circ$ is $360^\circ-285^\circ=75^\circ$ west of north, and Greg's bearing is $30^\circ$ east of north. So
$$\angle GPR=75^\circ+30^\circ=105^\circ.$$

questions.question:
Ringo and Greg start at location $P$ and drive in different directions. Ringo drives at a speed of 70 km/h on a bearing of $285^\circ$, while Greg drives at a speed of 60 km/h on a bearing of $030^\circ$, as shown in the diagram.

Given that $\angle GPR=105^\circ$, what will be the distance between Ringo and Greg after travelling for 2 hours? Give your answer correct to the nearest kilometre.
questions.answer:
After 2 hours, Ringo has travelled $140$ km and Greg $120$ km. By the cosine rule,
$$d^2=140^2+120^2-2(140)(120)\cos105^\circ=42696.199\ldots$$
$$d=206.63\ldots\approx207\text{ km}$$

questions.question:
A particle moves in a straight line. At time $t$ seconds, its distance $x$ metres from a fixed point $O$ on the line is given by $x=1-\cos(2t)$, for $0\le t\le\pi$.

Sketch the graph of $x$ as a function of $t$ for $0\le t\le\pi$.
questions.answer: $x=1-\cos2t$ has amplitude 1, period $\dfrac{2\pi}{2}=\pi$, centre line $x=1$. It starts at $x=0$ when $t=0$, rises to a maximum $x=2$ at $t=\frac\pi2$ (passing $x=1$ at $t=\frac\pi4$), and returns to $x=0$ at $t=\pi$.

questions.question:
A particle moves in a straight line. At time $t$ seconds, its distance $x$ metres from a fixed point $O$ on the line is given by $x=1-\cos(2t)$, for $0\le t\le\pi$.

Using the graph of $x$ against $t$, or otherwise, find the times when the particle is at rest and the position of the particle at these times.
questions.answer:
The particle is at rest when $v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2\sin2t=0$, i.e. at the stationary points of the graph:
$$t=0,\ \frac\pi2,\ \pi.$$
The positions at these times are $x=0,\ 2,\ 0$ metres respectively.

questions.question:
A particle moves in a straight line. At time $t$ seconds, its distance $x$ metres from a fixed point $O$ on the line is given by $x=1-\cos(2t)$, for $0\le t\le\pi$.

Find the velocity of the particle when $t=\dfrac\pi4$.
questions.answer: $v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2\sin2t$. At $t=\frac\pi4$: $v=2\sin\frac\pi2=2$ m/s.

questions.question:
A particle moves in a straight line. At time $t$ seconds, its distance $x$ metres from a fixed point $O$ on the line is given by $x=1-\cos(2t)$, for $0\le t\le\pi$.

When is the particle's velocity greater than 1 m/s?
questions.answer:
$v=2\sin2t$. Solve $2\sin2t=1$: $\sin2t=\frac12$, so for $0\le2t\le2\pi$,
$$2t=\frac\pi6,\ \frac{5\pi}6\ \Rightarrow\ t=\frac{\pi}{12},\ \frac{5\pi}{12}.$$
From the graph of $v$ (positive on $0<t<\frac\pi2$), $v>1$ for
$$\frac{\pi}{12}<t<\frac{5\pi}{12}.$$

questions.question:
Consider the curve $y=x^3-6x^2+9x+3$.

Find the location and nature of any stationary points.
questions.answer:
$y'=3x^2-12x+9$, $y''=6x-12$.

Stationary points: $3x^2-12x+9=0\Rightarrow x^2-4x+3=0\Rightarrow(x-1)(x-3)=0\Rightarrow x=1$ or $x=3$.

- $x=1$: $y=1-6+9+3=7$, $y''=-6<0$ (concave down) $\Rightarrow$ local maximum at $(1,7)$.
- $x=3$: $y=27-54+27+3=3$, $y''=6>0$ (concave up) $\Rightarrow$ local minimum at $(3,3)$.

questions.question:
Consider the curve $y=x^3-6x^2+9x+3$.

Find the point of inflection.

Consider the curve $y=x^3-6x^2+9x+3$. It has a local maximum at $(1,7)$, a local minimum at $(3,3)$ and a point of inflection at $(2,5)$.

Sketch the curve, labelling the stationary points, the point of inflection and the $y$-intercept. The $x$-intercepts are not required.
questions.answer: $y$-intercept: $y(0)=3$, so $(0,3)$. The curve is a positive cubic: it rises to the local maximum $(1,7)$, falls through the point of inflection $(2,5)$ to the local minimum $(3,3)$, then rises again. (It crosses the $x$-axis once, at some $x<0$.)

questions.question: Prove that $\sec x+\tan x=\dfrac{\cos x}{1-\sin x}$.
questions.answer: $$\text{LHS}=\frac{1}{\cos x}+\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}=\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}=\frac{(1+\sin x)(1-\sin x)}{\cos x(1-\sin x)}=\frac{1-\sin^2x}{\cos x(1-\sin x)}=\frac{\cos^2x}{\cos x(1-\sin x)}=\frac{\cos x}{1-\sin x}=\text{RHS}$$

questions.question: Given that $\sec x+\tan x=\dfrac{\cos x}{1-\sin x}$, find the exact value of $\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac\pi3}(\sec x+\tan x)\,dx$.
questions.answer:
Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}(1-\sin x)=-\cos x$,
$$\int_0^{\frac\pi3}\frac{\cos x}{1-\sin x}\,dx=-\Big[\ln|1-\sin x|\Big]_0^{\frac\pi3}=-\ln\left(1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)+\ln1$$
$$=-\ln\frac{2-\sqrt3}{2}=\ln\frac{2}{2-\sqrt3}\ \left(=\ln(4+2\sqrt3)\right).$$

questions.question:
$ABC$ is a triangle. The numbers $1+\sin A,\ \dfrac12,\ 1-\sin A$ are the first three terms of a geometric sequence.

Find the possible values of $A$.
questions.answer:
For a GP the ratios are equal:
$$\frac{\frac12}{1+\sin A}=\frac{1-\sin A}{\frac12}\ \Rightarrow\ (1-\sin A)(1+\sin A)=\frac14\ \Rightarrow\ 1-\sin^2A=\frac14\ \Rightarrow\ \cos^2A=\frac14$$
$\cos A=\pm\frac12$, and since $A$ is an angle of a triangle, $0<A<\pi$:
$$A=\frac\pi3\ \text{ or }\ A=\frac{2\pi}{3}.$$

questions.question:
$ABC$ is a triangle. The numbers $1+\sin A,\ \dfrac12,\ 1-\sin A$ are the first three terms of a geometric sequence. (The possible values of $A$ are $\dfrac\pi3$ and $\dfrac{2\pi}3$.)

Show that the limiting sum of the series $(1+\sin A)+\dfrac12+(1-\sin A)+\cdots$ exists.
questions.answer:
For $A=\frac\pi3$ or $\frac{2\pi}3$, $\sin A=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$. The common ratio is
$$r=\frac{1-\sin A}{\frac12}=2\left(1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)=2-\sqrt3\approx0.268.$$
Since $|r|<1$, the limiting sum exists.

questions.question:
The lifetime, $X$, in **tens** of hours, of a battery has a cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ given by
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}0, & x<1\\[2pt] \dfrac{25}{116}\left(x^2+3x-4\right), & 1\le x<1.8\\[2pt] 1, & x\ge1.8\end{cases}$$

Sketch the cumulative distribution function.
questions.answer: $F(x)=0$ for $x<1$. On $1\le x<1.8$, $F$ is an increasing, concave-up parabolic arc from $F(1)=\frac{25}{116}(1+3-4)=0$ to $F(1.8)=\frac{25}{116}(3.24+5.4-4)=\frac{25}{116}(4.64)=1$. Then $F(x)=1$ for $x\ge1.8$ (horizontal line).

questions.question:
The lifetime, $X$, in **tens** of hours, of a battery has a cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ given by
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}0, & x<1\\[2pt] \dfrac{25}{116}\left(x^2+3x-4\right), & 1\le x<1.8\\[2pt] 1, & x\ge1.8\end{cases}$$

An outdoor lantern requires three batteries, all of which must be working, to operate. Three new batteries are inserted into the lantern.

Find the probability that the lantern will be working after 15 hours. Answer as a percentage, rounded to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
15 hours corresponds to $x=1.5$. For one battery:
$$P(X>1.5)=1-F(1.5)=1-\frac{25}{116}\left(1.5^2+3(1.5)-4\right)=1-\frac{25}{116}(2.75)=\frac{189}{464}$$
All three batteries must last more than 15 hours (independently):
$$\left(\frac{189}{464}\right)^3=0.06758\ldots\approx6.76\%$$

questions.question:
The lifetime, $X$, in **tens** of hours, of a battery has a cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ given by
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}0, & x<1\\[2pt] \dfrac{25}{116}\left(x^2+3x-4\right), & 1\le x<1.8\\[2pt] 1, & x\ge1.8\end{cases}$$

Find the probability density function of the random variable $X$.
questions.answer:
$f(x)=F'(x)$:
$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{25}{116}(x^2+3x-4)\right]=\frac{25}{116}(2x+3)$$
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{25}{116}(2x+3), & 1\le x\le1.8\\[2pt] 0, & \text{elsewhere}\end{cases}$$

questions.question:
The average life cycle of an insect is one month. A viable nest of this insect has between 100 000 and 500 000 insects. The population $P$ of a nest of this insect grows so that
$$\frac{dP}{dt}=1200e^{0.3t},$$
where $t$ is in months.

A nest of these insects had a population of 5000 after one month. Determine how long it will take the nest to reach the viable stage of at least 100 000. Answer correct to the nearest month.
questions.answer:
$$P=\frac{1200}{0.3}e^{0.3t}+C=4000e^{0.3t}+C$$
$P=5000$ when $t=1$: $5000=4000e^{0.3}+C\Rightarrow C=-399.435\ldots$

For $P=100\,000$:
$$4000e^{0.3t}=100\,399.435\ldots\ \Rightarrow\ e^{0.3t}=25.0998\ldots\ \Rightarrow\ 0.3t=\ln25.0998\ldots$$
$$t=10.74\ldots\approx11$$
The nest reaches the viable stage after about **11 months**.

questions.question:
Harvey is designing an open-ended tent as shown below. The frame of the tent is made using rods of two different lengths:

- $x$ metres for the top and bottom edges
- $y$ metres for each sloping edge.

The rods cost \$9.50 per metre. The frame is covered by one rectangular sheet of fabric whose area is $24\text{ m}^2$.

Show that the total length, $l$ m, of rods is given by $l=3x+\dfrac{48}{x}$.
questions.answer:
The fabric is one rectangle measuring $x$ by $2y$ (it runs over both sloping sides):
$$x\times2y=24\ \Rightarrow\ y=\frac{12}{x}$$
The frame has 3 rods of length $x$ (ridge and two bottom edges) and 4 sloping rods of length $y$:
$$l=3x+4y=3x+4\times\frac{12}{x}=3x+\frac{48}{x}$$

questions.question:
Harvey is designing an open-ended tent as shown below. The frame of the tent is made using rods of two different lengths:

- $x$ metres for the top and bottom edges
- $y$ metres for each sloping edge.

The rods cost \$9.50 per metre. The frame is covered by one rectangular sheet of fabric whose area is $24\text{ m}^2$. The total length of rods is $l=3x+\dfrac{48}{x}$ metres.

Find the value of $x$ for which $l$ is a minimum.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{dl}{dx}=3-\frac{48}{x^2}=0\ \Rightarrow\ x^2=16\ \Rightarrow\ x=4\ (x>0)$$
$\dfrac{d^2l}{dx^2}=\dfrac{96}{x^3}=\dfrac{96}{64}>0$ at $x=4$, so $l$ is a minimum when $x=4$ m.

questions.question:
Harvey is designing an open-ended tent as shown below. The frame of the tent is made using rods of two different lengths:

- $x$ metres for the top and bottom edges
- $y$ metres for each sloping edge.

The rods cost \$9.50 per metre. The frame is covered by one rectangular sheet of fabric whose area is $24\text{ m}^2$. The total length of rods is $l=3x+\dfrac{48}{x}$ metres, which is a minimum when $x=4$.

What is the minimum cost of the frame?
The graph of $f(x)=3^{2x}-10(3^x)+9$ is shown below. Find the exact value of the area shaded (the region between the curve and the $x$-axis below the axis).
questions.answer:
**$x$-intercepts.** Let $u=3^x$: $u^2-10u+9=0\Rightarrow(u-9)(u-1)=0\Rightarrow u=1,9$, so $3^x=1$ or $3^x=9$, i.e. $x=0,\ 2$.

**Area.** The region lies below the $x$-axis on $0\le x\le2$, so
$$A=\left|\int_0^2\left(3^{2x}-10(3^x)+9\right)dx\right|=\left|\left[\frac{3^{2x}}{2\ln3}-\frac{10(3^x)}{\ln3}+9x\right]_0^2\right|$$
$$=\left|\left(\frac{81}{2\ln3}-\frac{90}{\ln3}+18\right)-\left(\frac{1}{2\ln3}-\frac{10}{\ln3}\right)\right|=\left|\frac{40}{\ln3}-\frac{80}{\ln3}+18\right|=\left|\frac{18\ln3-40}{\ln3}\right|$$
$$A=\frac{40-18\ln3}{\ln3}\text{ units}^2\ (\approx18.41)$$

questions.question: The graph of $y=x^2+4x+7$ is reflected about the $y$-axis, followed by a translation of 2 units to the right. Which of the following is the equation of the new graph?
questions.answer: Reflecting in the $y$-axis replaces $x$ with $-x$: $f(-x)$. Translating 2 units right replaces $x$ with $x-2$: $f(-(x-2))=f(-x+2)$. So $y=(-x+2)^2+4(-x+2)+7$ (B).

questions.question: If $x^2$, $4x+3$, $25$ are in a geometric sequence, what is the value of $x$?
The circle below has centre $O$, radius $\dfrac{3}{\pi}$ cm and arc length $MN=1$ cm. What is the exact area of the sector $MON$?
questions.answer: $l=r\theta$: $1=\dfrac3\pi\theta$, so $\theta=\dfrac\pi3$. $A=\dfrac12r^2\theta=\dfrac12\times\dfrac{9}{\pi^2}\times\dfrac\pi3=\dfrac{3}{2\pi}\ \text{cm}^2$ (A).

questions.question: The figure shows an accurate graph of $y=A+B\sin(Cx)$, where $x$ is measured in degrees and $A$, $B$ and $C$ are constants (the graph oscillates between $-1$ and $3$, with a period of $120^\circ$ over $0\le x\le360^\circ$). Which of the following are the correct values of $A$, $B$ and $C$?
questions.answer: The graph lies between $-1$ and $3$, so the centre line is $y=1$ ($A=1$) and the amplitude is 2 ($B=2$). The period is $120^\circ$ (three cycles in $360^\circ$): $\dfrac{360}{C}=120$, so $C=3$ (B).

questions.question: At point $A$ (on a decreasing part of the curve, just before a point of inflection, where the graph is bending downwards), which of the following is true?
questions.answer: At $A$ the graph is decreasing, so $f'(x)<0$, and it is concave down (bending downwards as it approaches the point of inflection), so $f''(x)<0$ (D).

questions.question: What is the derivative of $e^x\ln(\cos x)$?
questions.answer: Product rule: $y'=e^x\ln(\cos x)+e^x\cdot\dfrac{-\sin x}{\cos x}=e^x(\ln(\cos x)-\tan x)$ (A).

questions.question: The points $(4,-6)$, $(7,4)$, $(10,7)$, $(13,2)$ lie on the continuous curve $y=f(x)$. Using the Trapezoidal Rule with 4 function values, which of the following is an estimate for $\displaystyle\int_4^{13}f(x)\,dx$?
questions.answer: With 4 function values there are 3 strips of width $h=3$: $\displaystyle\int_4^{13}f(x)\,dx\approx\dfrac{3}{2}\big[f(4)+f(13)+2(f(7)+f(10))\big]=\dfrac32\big[-6+2+2(4+7)\big]=\dfrac32(18)=27$ (C).

questions.question: The graph of an even function, $f(x)$, and an odd function, $g(x)$, are shown. Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ represent the shaded areas as shown. Which of the following expressions equals $\displaystyle\int_0^4 g(x)\,dx$?
questions.answer: Since $g$ is odd, its graph for $0\le x\le4$ is the reflection through the origin of its graph for $-4\le x\le0$. Shaded areas $A$, $B$ and $C$ then correspond to regions lying entirely below the $x$-axis between $x=0$ and $x=4$, so the integral is negative: $-(A+B+C)$ (B).

questions.question: A set of data is normally distributed with a mean of 48 and a standard deviation of 3. Approximately what percentage of the scores lie between 39 and 45?
A probability function is given by $P(X=x)=\dfrac{x+2}{14}$ for $x=0,1,2,3$. What is the variance of $P(x)$?
Given that $\dfrac{4x^3+x^{\frac52}}{\sqrt x}$ can be written in the form $4x^a+x^b$, find the value of $a$ and $b$.
Given that $\log_bx=2.6$ and $\log_by=4.2$, find the value of $\log_b\left(x^2\sqrt y\right)$.
Given $g(x)=2x^2+(k+4)x+k$, where $k$ is a real constant, find the discriminant, in simplest form, of $g(x)$ in terms of $k$.
The discriminant of $g(x)=2x^2+(k+4)x+k$ is $\Delta=k^2+16$, where $k$ is a real constant. Explain why $g(x)$ has two distinct real roots for all values of $k$.
questions.answer: Two distinct real roots require $\Delta>0$. Since $k^2\ge0$ for all real $k$, $k^2+16\ge16>0$. So $\Delta>0$ for all $k$, and $g(x)$ has two distinct real roots.

questions.question: A company has a structured salary scheme. Mahrukh's salary is reviewed every year. In year 1, Mahrukh earns \$28,000. In each of years 2, 3, …, 8 she receives a raise of \$1,500 per year. After year 8 the annual raise increases to \$2,500 per year, and she finishes on a salary of \$58,500 at the end of the scheme. What is Mahrukh's salary in year 8?
questions.answer: This is an arithmetic sequence with $a=28000$, $d=1500$: $T_8=28000+7(1500)=\$38\,500$.

questions.question: A company has a structured salary scheme. In year 1, Mahrukh earns \$28,000. In each of years 2, 3, …, 8 she receives a raise of \$1,500 per year (so her year 8 salary is \$38,500). After year 8 the annual raise increases to \$2,500 per year, and she finishes on a salary of \$58,500 at the end of the scheme. What is the total amount earned by Mahrukh over the entire scheme?

Jayden is doing a sponsored cycle. He plans to cycle 1000 km over a number of days. He plans to cycle 10 km on day 1 and increase the distance by 10% a day. How long will it take Jayden to complete the challenge?
questions.answer: A geometric series with $a=10$, $r=1.1$: $S_n=\dfrac{10(1.1^n-1)}{0.1}=100(1.1^n-1)\ge1000$. $1.1^n\ge11$, so $n\ge\dfrac{\log11}{\log1.1}=25.16$. It will take Jayden 26 days.

questions.question: In an arithmetic series, the 1st term is $-12$, the 17th term is 12 and the last term is 45. Find the sum of all the terms in the series.
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=5$ cm, $BC=8$ cm and $AC=7$ cm. Show that $\cos A=\dfrac17$.
questions.answer: Cosine rule: $\cos A=\dfrac{AB^2+AC^2-BC^2}{2(AB)(AC)}=\dfrac{25+49-64}{2\times5\times7}=\dfrac{10}{70}=\dfrac17$.

questions.question: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=5$ cm, $AC=7$ cm, $BC=8$ cm and $\cos A=\dfrac17$. By finding the exact value of $\sin A$, determine the exact value of the area of $\triangle ABC$.
questions.answer: $\sin^2A=1-\dfrac1{49}=\dfrac{48}{49}$, so $\sin A=\dfrac{\sqrt{48}}{7}=\dfrac{4\sqrt3}{7}$ (as $A$ is acute). Area $=\dfrac12(5)(7)\sin A=\dfrac{35}{2}\times\dfrac{4\sqrt3}{7}=10\sqrt3\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.question: Solve $2\cos^2x+3\cos x+1=0$ for $0\le x\le2\pi$.
questions.answer: Let $u=\cos x$: $2u^2+3u+1=(2u+1)(u+1)=0$, so $\cos x=-\dfrac12$ or $\cos x=-1$. $\cos x=-\dfrac12$: $x=\pi-\dfrac\pi3=\dfrac{2\pi}3$ or $x=\pi+\dfrac\pi3=\dfrac{4\pi}3$. $\cos x=-1$: $x=\pi$. So $x=\dfrac{2\pi}3,\ \pi,\ \dfrac{4\pi}3$.

questions.question: Show that $\dfrac{\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta+\sin\theta\cos\theta}=1-\tan\theta$.
questions.answer: LHS $=\dfrac{(\cos\theta-\sin\theta)(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)}{\cos\theta(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)}=\dfrac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=1-\tan\theta=$ RHS.

questions.question: The depth $d$ metres of a diver relative to the water surface is modelled by $d(t)=\cos\left(2t+\dfrac\pi3\right)-1$, where $t$ is measured in seconds. Sketch the graph of $d(t)$ for $0\le t\le2\pi$, labelling the coordinates of all intercepts.
questions.answer: The graph is a cosine curve with amplitude 1, centre line $d=-1$, period $\pi$ (two cycles in $0\le t\le2\pi$), shifted left by $\dfrac\pi6$. Vertical intercept: $d(0)=\cos\dfrac\pi3-1=-\dfrac12$, so $\left(0,-\dfrac12\right)$. The graph touches the $t$-axis ($d=0$, where $\cos(2t+\frac\pi3)=1$) at $\left(\dfrac{5\pi}6,0\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{11\pi}6,0\right)$. Minimum points $(-2)$ at $t=\dfrac\pi3$ and $\dfrac{4\pi}3$; the endpoint is $\left(2\pi,-\dfrac12\right)$ (see graph).

questions.question: The depth $d$ metres of a diver relative to the water surface is modelled by $d(t)=\cos\left(2t+\dfrac\pi3\right)-1$. Find the greatest and least values of $d$.
questions.answer: Since $-1\le\cos\left(2t+\frac\pi3\right)\le1$, $-2\le d\le0$. The greatest value of $d$ is 0 and the least value is $-2$.

questions.question: Differentiate $f(x)=x^2+3x$ using first principles.
questions.answer: $f(x+h)=(x+h)^2+3(x+h)=x^2+2xh+h^2+3x+3h$. $f'(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}\dfrac{2xh+h^2+3h}{h}=\lim_{h\to0}(2x+h+3)=2x+3$.

questions.question: A function is given by $y=-x^3+9x^2-24x+16$. Find any stationary points, determine their nature and find any point(s) of inflection.
questions.answer:
$y'=-3x^2+18x-24=-3(x-2)(x-4)$. Stationary points at $x=2$ and $x=4$: $y(2)=-8+36-48+16=-4$ and $y(4)=-64+144-96+16=0$, so $(2,-4)$ and $(4,0)$. $y''=-6x+18$.

At $x=2$: $y''=6>0$, concave up, so $(2,-4)$ is a local minimum. At $x=4$: $y''=-6<0$, concave down, so $(4,0)$ is a local maximum.

Inflection: $y''=0$ at $x=3$; $y''=6>0$ at $x=2$ and $y''=-6<0$ at $x=4$, so the concavity changes. $y(3)=-27+81-72+16=-2$, so $(3,-2)$ is a point of inflection.

questions.question: A function is given by $y=-x^3+9x^2-24x+16$, with a local minimum at $(2,-4)$, a local maximum at $(4,0)$ and a point of inflection at $(3,-2)$. Sketch the curve, labelling these points and the $y$-intercept.
questions.answer: The $y$-intercept is $(0,16)$. The curve comes from the top left (a negative cubic), decreases to the local minimum $(2,-4)$ (passing through $(1,0)$, as $y=-(x-1)(x-4)^2$), rises through the inflection $(3,-2)$ to the local maximum $(4,0)$, which touches the $x$-axis, then decreases (see graph).

questions.question: A curve has the equation $y=\log_e(x^3-5)$. Find the equation of the normal to the curve at the point $x=2$.
questions.answer: $y'=\dfrac{3x^2}{x^3-5}$. At $x=2$: $y=\ln3$ and $y'=\dfrac{12}{3}=4$. The gradient of the normal is $-\dfrac14$. $y-\ln3=-\dfrac14(x-2)$, i.e. $y=-\dfrac14x+\dfrac12+\ln3$ (or $x+4y-4\ln3-2=0$).

questions.question: A function $g(x)=ax^2+\dfrac bx$ has a minimum value at $x=4$. It is also known that $g(4)=96$. Calculate the values of $a$ and $b$.
Find $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{e^{3x}}{e^{3x}+1}\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{e^{3x}}{e^{3x}+1}dx=\dfrac13\int\dfrac{3e^{3x}}{e^{3x}+1}dx=\dfrac13\ln(e^{3x}+1)+C$.

questions.question: Prove that $\sec^2x=1+\tan^2x$.
questions.answer: Starting from $\cos^2x+\sin^2x=1$ and dividing by $\cos^2x$: $1+\tan^2x=\sec^2x$.

questions.question: Using $\sec^2x=1+\tan^2x$, find $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/6}\tan^22x\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\tan^22x=\sec^22x-1$. $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/6}(\sec^22x-1)dx=\left[\dfrac12\tan2x-x\right]_0^{\pi/6}=\dfrac12\tan\dfrac\pi3-\dfrac\pi6=\dfrac{\sqrt3}2-\dfrac\pi6=\dfrac{3\sqrt3-\pi}6$.

questions.question: The curves $y=e^x$ and $y=e^{-x}$ are shown, with the horizontal line $y=e$ and vertical line $x=1$. $P$ is the lined region (bounded by $y=e$, $y=e^x$ and $y=e^{-x}$), and $Q$ is the solid shaded region. Find the area of the entire lined region $P$.
questions.answer: By symmetry about the $y$-axis, Area $P=2\displaystyle\int_0^1(e-e^x)\,dx=2\left[ex-e^x\right]_0^1=2\big[(e-e)-(0-1)\big]=2\ \text{u}^2$.

questions.question: The curves $y=e^x$ and $y=e^{-x}$ are shown, with the vertical line $x=1$. $Q$ is the solid shaded region between the two curves, from $x=0$ to $x=1$. Write an integral which could be used to find the area of $Q$. Do not solve this integral.
questions.answer: Area of $Q=\displaystyle\int_0^1(e^x-e^{-x})\,dx$.

questions.question: The parabola $y=-x^2+6x-5$ meets the $x$-axis at $A(1,0)$ and $B(5,0)$. The line $y=-x+5$ meets the parabola at $C(2,3)$ and $B$. Find the area of the shaded region (bounded by the $y$-axis, the $x$-axis, the line from $(0,5)$ to $C$, and the parabola from $C$ down to $A$).
questions.answer: Shaded area $=\displaystyle\int_0^2(-x+5)\,dx-\int_1^2(-x^2+6x-5)\,dx$. First: $\left[-\dfrac{x^2}2+5x\right]_0^2=-2+10=8$. Second: $\left[-\dfrac{x^3}3+3x^2-5x\right]_1^2=\left(-\dfrac83+12-10\right)-\left(-\dfrac13+3-5\right)=-\dfrac23+\dfrac73=\dfrac53$. Area $=8-\dfrac53=\dfrac{19}3\ \text{u}^2$.

questions.question: The diagram shows the graph of $y=f'(x)$, the derivative of $y=f(x)$. For what values of $x$ is the curve $y=f(x)$ increasing?
questions.answer: $f(x)$ is increasing where $f'(x)>0$, which occurs when $x<-2$.

questions.question: The diagram shows the graph of $y=f'(x)$, the derivative of $y=f(x)$ (it crosses the $x$-axis at $x=-2$ and touches it at $x=3$). Sketch a possible graph of $y=f(x)$.
questions.answer: $f'(x)>0$ for $x<-2$, $=0$ at $x=-2$ and $<0$ for $-2<x<3$: $f$ increases then has a local maximum at $x=-2$. At $x=3$, $f'(x)=0$ and $f'$ is negative on both sides, so $f$ has a horizontal point of inflection at $x=3$ (concave up to concave down), and $f$ is decreasing for all $x>-2$. A possible graph is shown (it may be translated vertically).

questions.question: Find $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\sqrt x+1\right)^3$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sqrt x+1)^3=3(\sqrt x+1)^2\cdot\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt x}=\dfrac{3(\sqrt x+1)^2}{2\sqrt x}$.

questions.question: Given that $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\sqrt x+1\right)^3=\dfrac{3(\sqrt x+1)^2}{2\sqrt x}$, find $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{(\sqrt x+1)^2}{2\sqrt x}\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{3(\sqrt x+1)^2}{2\sqrt x}dx=(\sqrt x+1)^3+c$, so $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{(\sqrt x+1)^2}{2\sqrt x}dx=\dfrac13(\sqrt x+1)^3+C$.

questions.question: A factory assembles torches. Each torch requires one battery and one bulb. It is known that 6% of all batteries and 4% of all bulbs are defective. Find the probability that, if a torch is selected at random, both the battery and the bulb are not defective. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer: The events are independent: $P(\text{both OK})=(1-0.06)(1-0.04)=0.94\times0.96=0.9024\approx0.90$.

questions.question: A pizza shop estimates that the time $X$ hours to deliver a pizza from when it is ordered is a continuous random variable with probability density function $f(x)=\dfrac43-\dfrac23x$ for $0<x<1$, and 0 otherwise. What is the probability of the pizza being delivered within half an hour of being ordered?
questions.answer: $P(X\le0.5)=\displaystyle\int_0^{0.5}\left(\dfrac43-\dfrac23x\right)dx=\left[\dfrac43x-\dfrac13x^2\right]_0^{0.5}=\dfrac23-\dfrac1{12}=\dfrac7{12}\approx0.5833$.

questions.question: The monthly sales $X$ (in units of \$100 000) of a business are modelled by the probability density function $f(x)=kx^3(1-x^2)$ for $0\le x\le1$, and 0 otherwise (Model 1). Determine the value of $k$.
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int_0^1k(x^3-x^5)dx=1$: $k\left[\dfrac{x^4}4-\dfrac{x^6}6\right]_0^1=k\left(\dfrac14-\dfrac16\right)=\dfrac k{12}=1$, so $k=12$.

questions.question: The monthly sales $X$ (in units of \$100 000) of a business are modelled by two probability density functions: Model 1, $f(x)=12x^3(1-x^2)$ for $0\le x\le1$; Model 2, $g(x)=2x$ for $0\le x\le1$ (both 0 otherwise). Show that the two models have the same median value.
questions.answer:
Model 2: $\displaystyle\int_0^m2x\,dx=m^2=\dfrac12$, so $m=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$.

Model 1: $\displaystyle12\int_0^m(x^3-x^5)dx=12\left(\dfrac{m^4}4-\dfrac{m^6}6\right)=3m^4-2m^6=\dfrac12$. At $m=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$: $m^4=\dfrac14$, $m^6=\dfrac18$, so $3\left(\dfrac14\right)-2\left(\dfrac18\right)=\dfrac34-\dfrac14=\dfrac12$ ✓. (Here $m$ is the only solution in $[0,1]$, since the CDF is increasing.) Both models have the same median, $m=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\approx0.707$.

questions.question: The weights of bags of red gravel may be modelled by a normal distribution with mean 25.8 kg and a standard deviation of 0.5 kg. What is the probability that a randomly selected bag will have a weight between 25.5 kg and 26.5 kg? (Use the standard normal table: $P(Z<1.4)=0.9192$, $P(Z<0.6)=0.7257$.)
A bus is uniformly late between 2 and 10 minutes. If the bus is late by more than 7 minutes, you will be late for school. What is the probability of you being late for school?
questions.answer: The lateness $X$ is uniformly distributed on $[2,10]$, a length of 8 minutes, so $f(x)=\dfrac18$. $P(X>7)=\dfrac{10-7}{8}=\dfrac38=0.375$.

questions.question: Find the global maximum and minimum values of $y=x^3-3x^2-9x+5$ for $-2\le x\le5$.
questions.answer: $y'=3x^2-6x-9=3(x-3)(x+1)=0$ gives $x=-1,\ 3$. $y(-1)=-1-3+9+5=10$ and $y(3)=27-27-27+5=-22$. Endpoints: $y(-2)=-8-12+18+5=3$ and $y(5)=125-75-45+5=10$. Comparing the values $3,\ 10,\ -22,\ 10$: the global maximum value is 10 (at $x=-1$ and $x=5$) and the global minimum value is $-22$ (at $x=3$).

questions.question: The diagram shows a cylinder of radius $x$ and height $y$ inscribed in a cone of radius $R$ and height $H$, where $R$ and $H$ are constants. The volume of a cone of radius $r$ and height $h$ is $\dfrac13\pi r^2h$ and the volume of a cylinder of radius $r$ and height $h$ is $\pi r^2h$. Show that the volume $V$ of the cylinder can be written as $V=\dfrac HR\pi x^2(R-x)$.
questions.answer: By similar triangles (the small cone above the cylinder is similar to the whole cone): $\dfrac{y}{R-x}=\dfrac HR$, so $y=\dfrac HR(R-x)$. $V=\pi x^2y=\pi x^2\cdot\dfrac HR(R-x)=\dfrac HR\pi x^2(R-x)$.

questions.question: A cylinder of radius $x$ is inscribed in a cone of radius $R$ and height $H$ (constants), with volume $V=\dfrac HR\pi x^2(R-x)$ for $0<x<R$. By considering the inscribed cylinder of maximum volume, show that the volume of any inscribed cylinder does not exceed $\dfrac49$ of the volume of the cone.
questions.answer:
$V=\dfrac{H\pi}{R}(Rx^2-x^3)$, so $V'=\dfrac{H\pi}R(2Rx-3x^2)=\dfrac{H\pi}Rx(2R-3x)$. $V'=0$ gives $x=0$ (not valid) or $x=\dfrac{2R}3$. $V''=\dfrac{H\pi}R(2R-6x)$; at $x=\dfrac{2R}3$, $V''=\dfrac{H\pi}R(2R-4R)=-2H\pi<0$, so this is a maximum.

Maximum volume: $V=\dfrac HR\pi\left(\dfrac{2R}3\right)^2\left(R-\dfrac{2R}3\right)=\dfrac HR\pi\cdot\dfrac{4R^2}9\cdot\dfrac R3=\dfrac49\left(\dfrac13\pi R^2H\right)=\dfrac49V_{\text{cone}}$.

Since this is the maximum, the volume of any inscribed cylinder does not exceed $\dfrac49$ of the volume of the cone.

questions.question: In a network audit, 58% of devices show a temperature alert, 46% show a humidity alert, and 31% show both alerts. A device is selected from those showing at least one of the two alerts. What is the probability that it shows exactly one alert?
questions.answer: $P(\text{at least one})=0.58+0.46-0.31=0.73$ and $P(\text{exactly one})=0.73-0.31=0.42$. The required probability is $\dfrac{0.42}{0.73}=\dfrac{42}{73}$ (B).

questions.question: How many solutions does $\sin\theta=\cos(2\theta)$ have in the interval $0\le\theta\le2\pi$?
questions.answer: $\cos2\theta=1-2\sin^2\theta$, so $2\sin^2\theta+\sin\theta-1=0$, i.e. $(2\sin\theta-1)(\sin\theta+1)=0$. $\sin\theta=\dfrac12$ gives $\theta=\dfrac\pi6,\dfrac{5\pi}6$; $\sin\theta=-1$ gives $\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}2$. Three solutions (C).

questions.question: A normally distributed random variable $X$ satisfies $P(X<42)=0.10$ and $P(X>58)=0.10$. The variable $Y$ is defined by $Y=100-2X$. What is $P(-16<Y<16)$?
Suppose $f(x)=\dfrac{ax+b}{cx+d}$, where $ad-bc\ne0$ and $c\ne0$. Which has the following properties?
questions.answer: $f(x)=\dfrac ac+\dfrac{k}{cx+d}$ with $k\ne0$ is a hyperbola: it has no turning points, a vertical asymptote at $x=-\dfrac dc$ and a horizontal asymptote $y=\dfrac ac$, and $x=-\dfrac dc$ is excluded from the domain. The only $y$-value never reached is $y=\dfrac ac$ (C).
options: The graph has exactly one turning point.
The graph has a vertical asymptote but no horizontal asymptote.
There is exactly one $y$-value that is not in the range of the function.
The graph has domain equal to all real numbers.

questions.question: Let $2^{2x}-5\cdot2^x+6=0$. Which of the following could be a value of $x$?

A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement $x$ metres at time $t$ seconds is implicitly defined by $t=x^3+3x$. What is the acceleration of the particle (in m s$^{-2}$) at the instant when $x=1$?
questions.answer: $\dfrac{dt}{dx}=3x^2+3$, so $v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\dfrac1{3x^2+3}$. $a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=\dfrac{dv}{dx}\cdot v=\dfrac{-6x}{(3x^2+3)^2}\cdot\dfrac1{3x^2+3}=-\dfrac{6x}{(3x^2+3)^3}$. At $x=1$: $a=-\dfrac{6}{216}=-\dfrac1{36}$ (B).

questions.question: The area bounded by the curve $y=\dfrac{x}{x^2+1}$, the $x$-axis, the $y$-axis and the vertical line $x=k$, where $k>0$, is exactly equal to $\ln5$ square units. What is the exact value of $k$?
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int_0^k\dfrac{x}{x^2+1}dx=\dfrac12\ln(k^2+1)=\ln5$, so $k^2+1=25$ and $k^2=24$, $k=2\sqrt6$ (A).

questions.question: The graph of a differentiable function $y=f(x)$ passes through the point $(2,1)$ and has a stationary point at $(5,8)$. A new function $g(x)$ is defined by $g(x)=[f(x)]^2f(2x-2)$. Find the exact value of $g'(2)$.

A student deposits \$800 at the end of each month for 18 months into an account earning 6% p.a. compounded monthly. No further deposits are made, but the money remains invested for another 6 months. Which expression gives the value of the account after 24 months?
questions.answer: The monthly rate is $\dfrac{6\%}{12}=0.5\%$. After 18 deposits the future value is $800\left(\dfrac{1.005^{18}-1}{0.005}\right)$, which then grows for 6 more months: multiply by $1.005^6$ (D).

questions.question: Using first principles, differentiate $f(x)=2x^2-5x+3$.
Evaluate the definite integral, leaving your answer in exact form: $\displaystyle\int_1^4\left(\dfrac2{3x-2}+\dfrac1{\sqrt x}\right)dx$.
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int_1^4\left(\dfrac2{3x-2}+x^{-1/2}\right)dx=\left[\dfrac23\ln(3x-2)+2\sqrt x\right]_1^4=\left(\dfrac23\ln10+4\right)-\left(\dfrac23\ln1+2\right)=2+\dfrac23\ln10$.

questions.question: The number of clips a wildlife camera records each night forms an arithmetic sequence. Over the first 10 nights the camera records a total of 730 clips. On the tenth night it records 100 clips. Show the number of clips recorded on the first night is 46.
The number of clips a wildlife camera records each night forms an arithmetic sequence. The first night records 46 clips and the tenth night records 100. Find the common difference.

The number of clips a wildlife camera records each night forms an arithmetic sequence with first term 46 and common difference 6. Assuming the same pattern continues, find the first night by which the total number of clips recorded exceeds 1200.

The time $T$, in seconds, for a humidity sensor to stabilise after each misting cycle is normally distributed with mean 18.5 seconds and standard deviation 2.4 seconds. A cycle is classified as delayed if the stabilisation time is more than 22.1 seconds. During a week, the system completes 360 misting cycles. Estimate the number of delayed cycles in that week.
questions.answer: $z=\dfrac{22.1-18.5}{2.4}=1.5$. $P(Z>1.5)=1-0.9332=0.0668$. Expected number $=360\times0.0668\approx24$ delayed cycles.

questions.question: Solve for $x$: $\log_{\frac13}(2x-1)+\log_3(x-3)=-1$.
questions.answer: $\log_{1/3}(2x-1)=-\log_3(2x-1)$. So $\log_3\dfrac{x-3}{2x-1}=-1$, giving $\dfrac{x-3}{2x-1}=\dfrac13$, so $3x-9=2x-1$ and $x=8$. Check the domain ($x>3$): $x=8$ is valid.

questions.question: A box contains one fair die and one special die. The special die has $P(6)=\dfrac13$ and $P(1)=P(2)=P(3)=P(4)=P(5)=\dfrac2{15}$. One die is chosen at random and then rolled twice. The same die is used for both rolls. Given that the first roll is a 6, find the probability that the special die was chosen.
questions.answer: $P(\text{special}\mid6)=\dfrac{\frac12\cdot\frac13}{\frac12\cdot\frac13+\frac12\cdot\frac16}=\dfrac{1/6}{1/6+1/12}=\dfrac23$.

questions.question: A box contains one fair die and one special die. The special die has $P(6)=\dfrac13$ and $P(1)=P(2)=P(3)=P(4)=P(5)=\dfrac2{15}$. One die is chosen at random and rolled twice (the same die is used for both rolls). Given that the first roll is a 6, find the probability that the second roll is even.
questions.answer: Given a first roll of 6, the special die was chosen with probability $\dfrac23$ and the fair die with probability $\dfrac13$. Special die: $P(\text{even})=\dfrac2{15}+\dfrac2{15}+\dfrac13=\dfrac35$. Fair die: $\dfrac12$. $P(\text{even})=\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac35+\dfrac13\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac25+\dfrac16=\dfrac{17}{30}$.

questions.question: A box contains one fair die and one special die. The special die has $P(6)=\dfrac13$ and $P(1)=P(2)=P(3)=P(4)=P(5)=\dfrac2{15}$. One die is chosen at random and then rolled twice, using the same die for both rolls. A game pays \$18 if both rolls are sixes, \$6 if exactly one roll is a six, and nothing otherwise. Determine the entry fee that will make the game fair.
questions.answer: Fair die: $P(\text{two 6s})=\dfrac1{36}$, $P(\text{exactly one 6})=2\cdot\dfrac16\cdot\dfrac56=\dfrac5{18}$. Special die: $P(\text{two 6s})=\dfrac19$, $P(\text{exactly one 6})=2\cdot\dfrac13\cdot\dfrac23=\dfrac49$. Overall: $P(66)=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac1{36}+\dfrac19\right)=\dfrac5{72}$; $P(\text{one 6})=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac5{18}+\dfrac49\right)=\dfrac{13}{36}$. $E=18\cdot\dfrac5{72}+6\cdot\dfrac{13}{36}=\dfrac54+\dfrac{13}6=\dfrac{41}{12}\approx\$3.42$. A fair game has an entry fee of about \$3.42.

questions.question: The graph of $f(x)=x^2$ is dilated vertically by a scale factor of $k$, translated $m$ units to the right, and then translated 3 units up. The resulting graph is then reflected in the $x$-axis to form the final function $g(x)=-2x^2+8x-11$. Find the values of $m$ and $k$, where $k>0$.
questions.answer: The transformations give $y=k(x-m)^2+3$, then reflecting in the $x$-axis: $g(x)=-k(x-m)^2-3$. Completing the square: $-2x^2+8x-11=-2(x^2-4x)-11=-2(x-2)^2-3$. So $k=2$ and $m=2$.

questions.question: A remote observatory records the causes of 100 interruptions and the mean downtime associated with each cause: Network handover, 36 interruptions, 5 min; Sensor recalibration, 24, 12 min; Blocked lens, 18, 25 min; Battery replacement, 12, 40 min; Weather interference, 10, 18 min. A proposed upgrade can eliminate 70% of the interruptions (downtime) from exactly one cause. Installing the upgrade itself creates 90 minutes of downtime. If the objective is to maximise the net reduction in expected total downtime, determine which cause should be selected and the net reduction.
questions.answer: Total downtime per cause = number $\times$ mean downtime: Network handover $36\times5=180$ min; Sensor recalibration $24\times12=288$; Blocked lens $18\times25=450$; Battery replacement $12\times40=480$; Weather interference $10\times18=180$. Eliminating 70% gives reductions of 126, 201.6, 315, 336 and 126 minutes respectively. Subtracting the 90 minutes created by the upgrade, the largest net reduction is for Battery replacement: $336-90=246$ minutes.

questions.question: Using the trapezoidal rule with four sub-intervals, find an approximate value for $\displaystyle\int_1^3\dfrac{2\ln x}{x\sqrt{1+(\ln x)^2}}\,dx$, correct to 4 decimal places.
By using the product rule, show that the derivative of $y=x^3\ln x$ is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^2(3\ln x+1)$.
questions.answer: $u=x^3$, $v=\ln x$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2\ln x+x^3\cdot\dfrac1x=3x^2\ln x+x^2=x^2(3\ln x+1)$.

questions.question: Given that $\dfrac d{dx}\left(x^3\ln x\right)=x^2(3\ln x+1)$, find the exact value of $\displaystyle\int_1^ex^2\ln x\,dx$ in simplified exact form.
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int_1^e(3x^2\ln x+x^2)dx=\left[x^3\ln x\right]_1^e=e^3$. So $3\int_1^ex^2\ln x\,dx=e^3-\int_1^ex^2dx=e^3-\dfrac{e^3-1}3=\dfrac{2e^3+1}3$, and $\displaystyle\int_1^ex^2\ln x\,dx=\dfrac{2e^3+1}9$.

questions.question: Consider the cubic curve $y=x^3-3kx$, where $k$ is a positive constant. A tangent is drawn to the curve at a point $P$ in the first quadrant. This tangent is parallel to the line $y=9x+2$. Show that the $x$-coordinate of point $P$ is $x=\sqrt{k+3}$.
questions.answer: $y'=3x^2-3k$. The tangent is parallel to $y=9x+2$, so $3x^2-3k=9$, $x^2=k+3$. In the first quadrant $x>0$, so $x=\sqrt{k+3}$.

questions.question: A point $P$ in the first quadrant on the curve $y=x^3-3kx$ ($k>0$) has $x$-coordinate $\sqrt{k+3}$. Show that the $y$-coordinate of $P$ can be expressed as $y=(3-2k)\sqrt{k+3}$.

The point $P\left(\sqrt{k+3},\,(3-2k)\sqrt{k+3}\right)$ lies on $y=x^3-3kx$ and the tangent at $P$ has gradient 9. A normal to the curve at $P$ intersects the $y$-axis at $(0,b)$. Show that $b=\left(\dfrac{28}9-2k\right)\sqrt{k+3}$.
questions.answer: The tangent has gradient 9, so the normal has gradient $-\dfrac19$. The normal: $y-(3-2k)\sqrt{k+3}=-\dfrac19\left(x-\sqrt{k+3}\right)$. At $x=0$: $b=(3-2k)\sqrt{k+3}+\dfrac19\sqrt{k+3}=\left(\dfrac{28}9-2k\right)\sqrt{k+3}$.

questions.question: A loan of \$180 000 is to be repaid with equal monthly repayments of \$$M$ made at the end of each month. The initial interest rate is 6% p.a., compounded monthly. Show that the balance remaining after 3 months is $A_3=180\,000(1.005)^3-M\left(1+1.005+1.005^2\right)$.

A loan of \$180 000 is repaid with equal monthly repayments $M$ at the end of each month, with interest 6% p.a. compounded monthly, so that $A_n=180\,000(1.005)^n-M\dfrac{1.005^n-1}{0.005}$. Find the monthly repayment \$$M$ required to fully repay the loan after 180 months. Give your answer to the nearest cent.

A loan of \$180 000 is repaid with monthly repayments of \$1518.94 at the end of each month, with interest 6% p.a. compounded monthly. Find the outstanding balance immediately after the 120th repayment.

A loan has a balance of about \$78 568 immediately after the 120th repayment, with 60 monthly repayments remaining. The interest rate rises to 7.8% p.a., compounded monthly. Find the new monthly repayment required so that the loan is still fully repaid after the 180 months in total.

The population $P(t)$ of an endangered species is modelled by $\ln\left(\dfrac{P(t)}{3000-P(t)}\right)=0.2t-c$, where $t$ is the time in years and $c$ is a constant. Initially, when $t=0$, the population is 500. Find the exact time $t$ when the population reaches 2500.

The population $P(t)$ of an endangered species is modelled by $\ln\left(\dfrac{P(t)}{3000-P(t)}\right)=0.2t-\ln5$, with $P(0)=500$. Sketch the graph of $P(t)$ against $t$ for $t\ge0$. Clearly show all important features.
questions.answer: Rearranging: $\dfrac{P}{3000-P}=\dfrac{e^{0.2t}}5$, so $P(t)=\dfrac{3000}{1+5e^{-0.2t}}$. The graph starts at $(0,500)$, increases, with the steepest growth (point of inflection) when $P=1500$, at $t=5\ln5\approx8.05$, and approaches the horizontal asymptote $P=3000$ as $t\to\infty$ (a logistic curve; see graph). It passes through $(10\ln5,\,2500)\approx(16.1,\,2500)$.

questions.question: For values of $\theta$ for which it is defined, let $E(\theta)=\dfrac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\dfrac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}$. State the values of $\theta$ in $0\le\theta\le2\pi$ for which $E(\theta)$ is not defined, and prove that $E(\theta)=2\sec\theta$ on its domain.
questions.answer:
The denominators are zero when $\cos\theta=0$ or $1+\sin\theta=0$. In $0\le\theta\le2\pi$: $\theta=\dfrac\pi2$ or $\theta=\dfrac{3\pi}2$.

On the domain: $E(\theta)=\dfrac{(1+\sin\theta)^2+\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\dfrac{2+2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\dfrac2{\cos\theta}=2\sec\theta$.

questions.question: Using $E(\theta)=2\sec\theta$, solve $E(\theta)=4\cos\theta$ for $0\le\theta\le2\pi$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac2{\cos\theta}=4\cos\theta$, so $\cos^2\theta=\dfrac12$, $\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$. $\theta=\dfrac\pi4,\ \dfrac{3\pi}4,\ \dfrac{5\pi}4,\ \dfrac{7\pi}4$.

questions.question: Let $E(\theta)=\dfrac{1+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\dfrac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=2\sec\theta$ (undefined at $\theta=\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac{3\pi}2$). For a real number $m$, determine all values of $m$ for which $E(\theta)=m+\cos\theta$ has exactly two solutions in $0\le\theta\le2\pi$.
questions.answer:
Let $x=\cos\theta$, $-1\le x\le1$, $x\ne0$. Then $\dfrac2x=m+x$, so $m=\dfrac2x-x=g(x)$, with $g'(x)=-\dfrac2{x^2}-1<0$ (decreasing on each part of its domain).

For $0<x\le1$: $g(1)=1$ and $g(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to0^+$, so $m\ge1$. Each $x\in(0,1)$ gives two values of $\theta$, and $x=1$ gives $\theta=0,2\pi$ (also two solutions), so $m\ge1$ gives exactly two solutions.

For $-1\le x<0$: $g(-1)=-1$ and $g(x)\to-\infty$ as $x\to0^-$, so $m\le-1$. Each $x\in(-1,0)$ gives two values of $\theta$, but $x=-1$ gives only $\theta=\pi$, so $m=-1$ is excluded: $m<-1$.

(Since $x^2+mx-2=0$ has roots of opposite sign, at most one root is in $[-1,1]$ for each case.) Therefore $m<-1$ or $m\ge1$.

questions.question: A calibration-drift score $X$ has probability density function $f(x)=k(x+1)$ for $-1\le x\le1$, $f(x)=k(3-x)$ for $1<x\le3$, and 0 otherwise. Find the value of $k$.
questions.answer: $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1k(x+1)dx+\int_1^3k(3-x)dx=1$: $2k+2k=4k=1$, so $k=\dfrac14$. (Alternatively, the density is a triangle with base 4 and height $2k$: $\dfrac12(4)(2k)=1$.)

questions.question: A calibration-drift score $X$ has probability density function $f(x)=\dfrac14(x+1)$ for $-1\le x\le1$, $f(x)=\dfrac14(3-x)$ for $1<x\le3$, and 0 otherwise. Find the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ for all real $x$.
questions.answer: For $-1\le x\le1$: $F(x)=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^x\dfrac14(t+1)dt=\dfrac{(x+1)^2}8$, so $F(1)=\dfrac12$. For $1<x\le3$: $F(x)=\dfrac12+\displaystyle\int_1^x\dfrac14(3-t)dt=\dfrac{-x^2+6x-1}8=1-\dfrac{(3-x)^2}8$. Hence $F(x)=0$ for $x<-1$; $\dfrac{(x+1)^2}8$ for $-1\le x\le1$; $1-\dfrac{(3-x)^2}8$ for $1<x\le3$; and $1$ for $x>3$.

questions.question: A calibration-drift score $X$ has cumulative distribution function $F(x)=\dfrac{(x+1)^2}8$ for $-1\le x\le1$, $F(x)=1-\dfrac{(3-x)^2}8$ for $1<x\le3$ (0 below $-1$, 1 above 3). Find the lower quartile $Q_1$, the upper quartile $Q_3$, and hence the inter-quartile range of $X$, in exact form.
questions.answer: $F(Q_1)=\dfrac14$: $\dfrac{(Q_1+1)^2}8=\dfrac14$, so $(Q_1+1)^2=2$ and $Q_1=\sqrt2-1$ (rejecting $-1-\sqrt2<-1$). $F(Q_3)=\dfrac34$: $1-\dfrac{(3-Q_3)^2}8=\dfrac34$, so $(3-Q_3)^2=2$ and $Q_3=3-\sqrt2$ (rejecting $3+\sqrt2>3$). $\text{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1=4-2\sqrt2$. (By symmetry about $x=1$, $Q_3=2-Q_1$.)

questions.question: A score $X$ has the symmetric triangular density $f(x)=\dfrac14(x+1)$ for $-1\le x\le1$ and $\dfrac14(3-x)$ for $1<x\le3$ (CDF: $F(x)=\dfrac{(x+1)^2}8$ on $[-1,1]$, $1-\dfrac{(3-x)^2}8$ on $(1,3]$), with inter-quartile range $4-2\sqrt2$. An engineering team proposes a normal model $Y$ whose mean is the same as the median of $X$ and whose inter-quartile range is the same as for $X$. Estimate $P(Y>2)$, and compare this with $P(X>2)$.
questions.answer: By symmetry the median of $X$ is 1, so $\mu_Y=1$. For a normal distribution the quartiles are at $z=\pm0.675$, so $\text{IQR}=1.35\sigma=4-2\sqrt2$ and $\sigma=\dfrac{4-2\sqrt2}{1.35}\approx0.868$. $P(Y>2)=P\left(Z>\dfrac{2-1}{0.868}\right)=P(Z>1.15)\approx0.125$. For $X$: $P(X>2)=1-F(2)=\dfrac{(3-2)^2}8=\dfrac18=0.125$. The two models give nearly identical values for this tail probability.

questions.question: The depth of water, $W$ metres, inside a tidal shipping canal is modelled by $W(t)=8+\sin t+\cos t$, where $t$ is the time in hours after high tide, for $0\le t\le\pi$. Find the coordinates of any stationary points on the curve $W(t)$ within the interval $0\le t\le\pi$, and determine their nature.
questions.answer: $W'(t)=\cos t-\sin t=0$ gives $\tan t=1$, so $t=\dfrac\pi4$ in $[0,\pi]$. $W\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)=8+\dfrac{\sqrt2}2+\dfrac{\sqrt2}2=8+\sqrt2$. $W''(t)=-\sin t-\cos t$, and $W''\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)=-\sqrt2<0$, so $\left(\dfrac\pi4,8+\sqrt2\right)$ is a local maximum.

questions.question: The depth of water inside a tidal canal is $W(t)=8+\sin t+\cos t$, for $0\le t\le\pi$. Find the point(s) of inflection.
questions.answer: $W''(t)=-\sin t-\cos t=0$ gives $\tan t=-1$, so $t=\dfrac{3\pi}4$ in $[0,\pi]$. $W\left(\dfrac{3\pi}4\right)=8+\dfrac{\sqrt2}2-\dfrac{\sqrt2}2=8$. Test: $W''(0)=-1<0$ and $W''(\pi)=1>0$, so the concavity changes (down to up). The point of inflection is $\left(\dfrac{3\pi}4,8\right)$.

questions.question: The depth of water in a tidal canal is $W(t)=8+\sin t+\cos t$, for $0\le t\le\pi$ (with $W''(t)=0$ only at $t=\dfrac{3\pi}4$). A cargo ship requires the water depth to be dropping at its absolute fastest rate. Find the exact value of $t$ when the ship should cross the sandbar.
questions.answer: The depth drops fastest when $W'(t)=\cos t-\sin t$ is most negative. $W'(0)=1$, $W'\left(\dfrac{3\pi}4\right)=-\sqrt2$, $W'(\pi)=-1$. $W'$ has its only stationary point at $t=\dfrac{3\pi}4$ ($W''=0$), and $W''$ changes from negative to positive there, so $W'$ has an absolute minimum $-\sqrt2$. The ship should cross at $t=\dfrac{3\pi}4$ hours.

questions.question: A drone's guidance system makes a sequence of correction flights with lengths $L_1,L_2,L_3,\dots$, where $L_1=AD$. Consecutive lengths $L_n$ and $L_{n+1}$ are two sides of a triangle in which the angle opposite $L_{n+1}$ is $\theta$ and the angle opposite $L_n$ is $110^\circ-\theta$, where $0^\circ<\theta<55^\circ$. Show that the correction lengths form a geometric sequence with $\dfrac{L_{n+1}}{L_n}=q$, $q=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sin(110^\circ-\theta)}$, and hence write $L_n$ in terms of $AD$, $q$ and $n$.
questions.answer: Sine rule: $\dfrac{L_n}{\sin(110^\circ-\theta)}=\dfrac{L_{n+1}}{\sin\theta}$, so $\dfrac{L_{n+1}}{L_n}=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sin(110^\circ-\theta)}=q$, a constant (independent of $n$), so the lengths form a geometric sequence with ratio $q$. Since $L_1=AD$, $L_n=AD\,q^{n-1}$.

questions.question: The correction flights form a geometric sequence $L_n=AD\,q^{n-1}$ with $0<q<1$ (since $110^\circ-\theta>\theta$, the sides satisfy $L_n>L_{n+1}$). Find the total limiting correction distance in terms of $AD$ and $q$.
questions.answer: $S_\infty=\dfrac{AD}{1-q}$, since $|q|<1$.

questions.question: The correction flights form a geometric sequence with first term $AD=350$ m and common ratio $q$, $0<q<1$. The limiting total correction distance must not exceed 900 metres. Calculate the maximum allowable value of $q$, correct to four decimal places.

prev.answer: $S_\infty=\dfrac{AD}{1-q}$, since $|q|<1$.

questions.question: Let $q=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sin(110^\circ-\theta)}$ for $0^\circ<\theta<55^\circ$, where $q$ is an increasing function of $\theta$ (do not prove this). The maximum allowable value of $q$ is $0.6111$. Determine the greatest allowable value of $\theta$ to the nearest degree. You may use $\sin(110^\circ-\theta)=\sin110^\circ\cos\theta-\cos110^\circ\sin\theta$.
questions.answer: At the greatest allowable $\theta$: $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\sin(110^\circ-\theta)}=0.6111$, so $\sin\theta=q(\sin110^\circ\cos\theta-\cos110^\circ\sin\theta)$ and $\sin\theta(1+q\cos110^\circ)=q\sin110^\circ\cos\theta$. $\tan\theta=\dfrac{q\sin110^\circ}{1+q\cos110^\circ}=\dfrac{0.6111(0.9397)}{1+0.6111(-0.3420)}=0.7260$, so $\theta\approx35.98^\circ\approx36^\circ$.

questions.question:
The function $f(x) = x^3$ is transformed to $g(x) = (x-2)^3 + 5$ by a horizontal translation of 2 units followed by a vertical translation of 5 units.

What are the directions of the two translations?
questions.answer: Replacing $x$ by $x - 2$ translates the graph **2 units right**, and adding $5$ translates it **5 units up**. **(B)**

questions.question: What is the derivative of $\dfrac{x}{\cos x}$?
questions.answer:
By the quotient rule with $u = x$, $v = \cos x$:
$$\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{x}{\cos x}\right) = \frac{\cos x \cdot 1 - x(-\sin x)}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{\cos x + x\sin x}{\cos^2 x}. \quad \textbf{(A)}$$

questions.question:
Let $h(x) = \dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}$, where $f(1) = 2$, $f'(1) = 4$, $g(1) = 8$ and $g'(1) = 12$.

What is the gradient of the tangent to the graph of $y = h(x)$ at $x = 1$?

The height of the tide in a harbour can be modelled using the sine function. The time between high tide and low tide is 6 hours.

Which of the following could be the function representing the height $h$ of the tide, where $t$ is the time in hours?
questions.answer:
High tide to low tide is half a period, so the period is $12$ hours. For $h = \sin(bt)$ the period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{b}$:
$$\frac{2\pi}{b} = 12 \implies b = \frac{\pi}{6}. \quad \textbf{(B)}$$

questions.question: If $f(x) = \sin^2(3 - x)$, then $f'(0)$ is equal to:
questions.answer:
By the chain rule (twice):
$$f'(x) = 2\sin(3 - x) \cdot \cos(3 - x) \cdot (-1) = -2\sin(3 - x)\cos(3 - x),$$
so $f'(0) = -2\sin(3)\cos(3)$. **(B)**

questions.question: Show that $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^3 x\right) = 3\sec^4 x - 3\sec^2 x$.
questions.answer:
By the chain rule, with $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan x) = \sec^2 x$:
$$\frac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^3 x\right) = 3\tan^2 x \sec^2 x.$$
Using $\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1$:
$$3\tan^2 x\sec^2 x = 3(\sec^2 x - 1)\sec^2 x = 3\sec^4 x - 3\sec^2 x.$$

questions.question: Find $\dfrac{d^2}{dx^2}\left(e^{x^2}\right)$.
questions.answer:
$$\frac{d}{dx}\left(e^{x^2}\right) = 2xe^{x^2}.$$
By the product rule:
$$\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\left(e^{x^2}\right) = 2e^{x^2} + 2x \cdot 2xe^{x^2} = 2e^{x^2}\left(1 + 2x^2\right).$$

questions.question: Differentiate $\log_e\left(\sin^3 x\right)$, writing your answer in simplest form.
questions.answer:
Using the log law, $\log_e(\sin^3 x) = 3\log_e(\sin x)$ (where $\sin x > 0$). So
$$\frac{d}{dx}\log_e\left(\sin^3 x\right) = 3 \cdot \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = 3\cot x.$$
(Or by the chain rule: $\dfrac{3\sin^2 x\cos x}{\sin^3 x} = 3\cot x$.)

questions.question:
The population of a herd of wild horses is given by
$$P(t) = 400 + 50\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t\right)$$
where $t$ is time in months.

Find all times during the first 12 months when the population equals 375 horses.
questions.answer:
$$400 + 50\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = 375 \implies \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{6}\right) = -\frac12.$$
For $0 \le t \le 12$, $\;0 \le \dfrac{\pi t}{6} \le 2\pi$, so
$$\frac{\pi t}{6} = \frac{2\pi}{3} \text{ or } \frac{4\pi}{3} \implies t = 4 \text{ or } t = 8.$$
The population is 375 horses after **4 months** and after **8 months**.

$$P(t) = 400 + 50\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}t\right)$$
where $t$ is time in months.

Sketch the graph of $P(t)$ for $0 \le t \le 12$.
